segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The proposed fiscal year 2027 National Expenditure Program is hereby called to order.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I would like to acknowledge the presidents of centers who are with us today.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Our Senate President Pro Tempore, Senator Vicente Soto,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Senators Erwin Tulfo, Senator Panfilo Laxon,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan, Senator Camille Villar,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you to our dear colleagues for joining us this morning.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: For the record, during the plenary session on June 3, 2026,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: yours truly was elected Chairperson of the Committee on Finance.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Considering that the committee is composed of 20 members,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: all Senators except the Senate President and the ex-official members

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: all were elected as regular members of the committee on June 17, 2026.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Further, August 24, 2026, the following senators were designated

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: as Chairpersons of the committee and will work

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: with the committee on sponsoring the budget of the respective assigned agencies.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Senators Bam Aquino, Senators Pia Cayetano, Senators Christopher Lorenz-Bongo,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Senators Risa Ontiveros, Senators Loren Legarda, Senators Francis Kiko Pangilinan,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Senators Erwin Tulfo, and Senators Joel Villanueva.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: At this juncture, let me direct the Committee's Secretary

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: to acknowledge our resource persons present for today.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: Undersecretary Mary Ann De La Vega,

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: From the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development, or DEPDEV,

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: and the President of the Philippine Institute for Development Studies, or PIDS,

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: And last but not the least, from the Banko Central ng Pilipinas, or BSP,

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: we have Governor Eli M. Remolona, Jr.,

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: and Attorney Arnold Cabanlit of the Anti-Money Laundering Council, or AMLC Secretariat.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Likewise, to Senator Babacuino, who joined us as well this morning.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, before we start, the Chair would like to give his opening statement,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: but also Governor Eli Remolona, or the BSP,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: has requested that he be excused earlier because they have monetary boards,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: so we will ask him to present first,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and if the Senators will have any concerns,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: you may prepare questions for Governor Remolona.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Dear colleagues, secretaries, and members of the Cabinet present here today,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: my fellow workers in government, members of the Media Civil Society,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: to all our fellow Filipinos, good morning to all of you.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: As we convene the Development Budget Coordination Committee, or the DBCC today,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: we undertake the solemn duty of deliberating the National Budget of 2027.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: As Chair of the Committee on Finance,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I reaffirm our steadfast commitment to deliver a budget that serves as a reflection of the genuine needs of our people,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Today, we go back to the basics.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Let's go back to the basic needs of our fellow citizens.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Health, education, food, livelihood, security, and proper infrastructure.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: And so that our projects will not be divided into pieces,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: we need a long-term, comprehensive infrastructure master plan

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: that connects our roads, railways, airports, seaports, and communities,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and supports the country's development for generations to come.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: These should remain at the heart of our priorities.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Yes, the budget process can be complex, filled with accounting terms and figures,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: but we must not lose sight of what those numbers are meant to accomplish.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Beyond economic buzzwords and elaborate theories,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: what our people need now is action on the part of their government,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: as the people we serve are not mere statistics on a piece of paper in a stack of reports.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: They are families, breadwinners, farmers, students, and citizens counting on their government to deliver.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: That is why we are helping.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The 2027 budget is a budget that will address the primary needs or basic needs of our citizens.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: This is where we fully agree with the budget message of President Bongbong Marcos,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: for when we invest in our people, we invest in the future of our nation.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We have witnessed the problems faced by our country,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: especially when it comes to corruption and the wrong use of the country's budget.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We hear your concerns and understand your feelings and calls for transparency and trust in the government.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: As the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Finance,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: we will not allow the country's budget to go to waste,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: to go to waste, and to go to the wrong hands.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Every penny, every cent should only go to the programs and projects

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: that are included in the budget proposal and the agenda discussed in the plenary.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: And the plan will serve the right purpose and the well-being of your citizens.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: As we formally begin these deliberations,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I want to underscore and emphasize our clear intention to go back to basics in crafting this budget.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: In going back to basics, we mean accountability.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: For every peso, we appropriate that is focused and clear-eyed

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: about the basic needs of the people such as health, education, infrastructure

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: that will generate quality jobs for the people and to put the food on the table.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Noong nakaraang taon, pinamunuan ni Senate President Win Gatchalian ang Senate

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: at mas accessible sa nakakarami ang budget process.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Ngayong taon, ipagpatuloy at paiigtingin pa natin ang mga nasimulan niyang reforma.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Kasama ng ating vice chairpersons at mga kasamahan sa Senado,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: iwawak si natin ang pagwawaldas, susuriin ang bawat programa,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Dahil back to basics, dapat may pananagutan sa bawat piso

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: at bawat sentimo ang ginagastos ng gobyerno.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Sa lahat ng mga naging kontrobersya, lalo na sa mga kwestyonabling flood control projects,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: hindi pwedeng maging business as usual na lamang ang ating budget process.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We must learn from our mistakes.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We must earn back the public's trust.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: And we must restore the integrity of this sacred mandate.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Here's how we can make this happen.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Any individual amendments should be made on the floor.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Pabantayan at ipagbabawal na natin ang anumang last-minute insertions sa Bicameral Conference Committee.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We will continue live-streaming the Bicameral Conference Committee

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and maintaining the Senate Budget Transparency Portal

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: for the public to see and appreciate how the budget evolves

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: titiyakin natin na ang ipamamahagi ay walang political branding o pakikialam.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We will also continue to work with civil society organizations and other stakeholders,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: patuloy natin pakikinggan ang kanilang mga pananaw at rekomendasyon

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: habang sinusuri natin ang mga programa at pondong hinihingi ng bawat ahensya.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: To better public service, not paralysis.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We must address irregularities and strengthen safeguards against abuse

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: while ensuring that legitimate infrastructure projects continue without the necessary delay.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Ang dapat natin pigilan ay korupsyon at anomalya, hindi ang pag-unlad.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Muli ang unang hakbang sa ating back-to-basics ay accountability.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Sunod naman ang pagtiyak na tama at napakalimutan.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Napapanuhon ang mga preridad na ating pagkakagastusan.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: kailangan ba talaga ang pondong ito?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: At sino ang mananagot kung hindi ito maipapatupad?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Lagi't lagi nating i-considera ang necessity at feasibility sa pagtalakay ng budget.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Hindi po ito para lamang pahirapan ang mga ahensya.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Dahil siguro alam naman po [unclear], ito po ang isa sa ating pangunahing legislative agenda.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Being the principal sponsor and author of the universal healthcare law,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: At the very outset of the Senate budget deliberation, I want to make our positions clear as Chairman of the Committee of Finance.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Again, reiterate that healthcare will be among our highest priorities.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: As the principal sponsor of this measure, I remain committed to seeing this promise to be fully realized.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: With the new leadership of the Department of Health and PhilHealth, we have a great opportunity to continue building a healthcare system that is truly accessible, affordable, and responsive.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We will scrutinize the proposed budget for the Health Facilities Enhancement Program to ensure that it strengthens local government hospitals like the provincial hospitals while expanding and improving primary care services across the country.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Dapat may doktor, nars, gamot, kagamitan, at serbisyong tunay na nila mapapakinabangan.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: For PhilHealth, every peso entrusted to them must result in stronger financial protection for its members.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We must also ensure that revenues earmarked by law for universal healthcare are fully allocated and released only for their intended purposes.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: More than a corporation, PhilHealth is an essential piece that forms part of our national healthcare system.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: It serves as a vessel for UHC to be felt by our people.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Makikipagtulungan po tayo sa bagong pamunan ng DOH at PhilHealth upang mapalawak pa ang zero-balance billing at matiyak ang mga kwalipikadong pasyente ay makatatanggap ng hospital services na walang iniintinding babaya rin.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Hindi tayo titigil sa pagsulong at patuloy na pagpapalawig ng mas komprehensibong benefit packages, hindi lamang para sa higit ng mga nangangailangan, kundi pati na rin sa mga mga gawa at middle-class families na regular na naguhulog, ngunit maaari pa rin mabaon sa gastusin kapag tinamaan ng malubhang karamdaman.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The recent habagat rains have once again shown us hindi uuwi.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We need infrastructure projects that complement each other, are technically sound, ready for implementation, and capable of delivering lasting benefits.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The government's identification of 39 potential sites for rainwater catchment facilities in Metro Manila is a step in this right direction.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Similar science-based solutions must be pursued across the country.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: This is why, precisely why we need a comprehensive and long-term infrastructure master plan or the Master Plan for Infrastructure and National Development or the MIND Act, which we have filed under Senate Bill No. 2 under the 20th Congress.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: This is what we also emphasized in our privileged speech yesterday on the eve of the DBCC, for the reason that we seek to earn the support of our experts and that is everyone in this room.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: To reiterate that what we mentioned yesterday, we must continue investing in good infrastructure that creates lasting opportunities long after the construction equipment has left.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The true measure of a road is not the number of kilometers paved, it is the number of people connected to their employment and livelihood.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The true measure of a master plan is not the number of projects listed on paper, it is the number of lives changed for development.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: ang bawat ahensya at bawat lugar.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Roads, bridges, flood control, irrigation, railways, ports, and other infrastructure must form part of one coherent plan based on the actual needs and long-term development of the country.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: At the same time, agriculture and food security must be forgotten.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.

segments.text: At the DBCC, we have a number of issues.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: In the DBCC briefing in Congress last week, I said that we worry a lot about inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: We know how inflation affects the purchasing power of Filipino families.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Indeed, surveys say that in people's minds,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: inflation is the leading indicator of their well-being.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: The main challenge we now face with regard to inflation is global supply shocks.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Since the start of the war in Iran, oil prices have risen sharply.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: As a consequence, our energy prices and our food prices went through the roof.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: There is little the BSP can do about the price of oil itself, because our tools are limited

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: to those coming from the supply side.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: With that limitation, we must focus on the second round effects of global supply shocks.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: To address inflation pressures, the BSP has already tightened monetary policy twice this year.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: These actions were carefully calibrated to help push inflation back towards our target

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: and to keep inflation expectations well anchored,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: while at the same time recognizing the current weakness in economic activity.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: While at the same time recognizing the current weakness in economic activity, recent data on inflation is much more punctual than any other recent videos.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: have been somewhat encouraging. Inflation has moderated in recent months, although it remains

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: well above our target of 3%. Looking ahead, we expect inflation to gradually move closer

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: to our target over the medium term. At the same time, we remain vigilant about the continued risks

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: to the inflation outlook. The Monetary Board stands ready to take the necessary measures

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: to fulfill our mandate. We also have a mandate for financial stability.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: In this regard, I am pleased to inform that the Philippine banking system remains strong

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: and resilient. Banks continue to be well capitalized, adequately provisioned,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: and supported by ample liquidity. Together with the country's solid external position,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: these strengths will continue to improve.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: These strengths provide important buffers against global challenges and uncertainties.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Overall, these developments support the macroeconomic assumptions

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: that underpin the proposed fiscal year 2027 national budget.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: With that, let me turn the floor over to Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoa,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: who will present a more detailed discussion of recent economic developments and macroeconomic

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you, Governor Remolona. Next, we'd like to call our Secretary.

segments.speaker: Senator Vicente C. Sotto III
segments.text: I think the BSP wants to continue with the presentation.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: I join the Governor in thanking and greeting good morning to our Senate President,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Win Gatchalian, our Chair of the Committee on Finance, Senator J.V. Ejercito,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: our Honorable Vice Chairpersons, and Senators.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: For the next few minutes, I will be providing a background, particularly our recent assessment

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and external sector performance of the country.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this will provide some background to the macroeconomic assumptions that have been reflected

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: when the 2027 budget has been formulated.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: So let me start with inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Here we show the inflation numbers.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The target for the inflation is an average of 3% every year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And if you look back last year in 2025,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we see here that inflation, for the most part, has been manageable.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In fact, it's been below that 3% inflation target.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this is due particularly to the benign food inflation and energy prices last year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this continued, these favorable inflation numbers continued during the first two months of 2026.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: However, the conflict in the Middle East since February,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and February, 2026, drove global oil prices higher.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this translated to significant spillover to domestic inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: As we can see, the inflation rapidly rose from 2.4% in February.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: It went to as high as 7.2% back in April.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But since then, it has gradually eased to 6.2% as of July of this year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: However, inflation continues to be well above the target of 3%,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: despite that moderation in the last three or four months.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The moderation that we have seen since the period,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: during the period May to July months,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: reflects, for the most part, lower global oil prices,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: as well as some improvement in food supply.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Now, what was the response of the B2B?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: What was the response of the B2B to this recent developments?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: For the B2B, the monetary policy shifted to a tightening stance,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: given the uptick in inflation and the increase in the inflation outlook.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The B2B decided to raise target policy rates from 4.25% by 25 basis points each,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: last April and again in June 2026.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This brings the policy rate to 4.75%.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Let me just note that, as mentioned by our committee chair and the governor,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the BSP Monetary Board will be meeting today, again, to assess monetary policy.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But we are constrained to speak about the decision until the announcement at 2.30 this afternoon.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: describing what we have done in the past, in the last two policy meetings,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we characterize this as a calibrated move by the BSP.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And the main purpose is really to anchor inflation expectations

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and reduce what we call spillover or second-round effects

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that could bring about a broader price pressure moving forward.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But equally important, and we highlight here,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Mr. Chair, is that this policy action, this measured policy action,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: is meant also to complement fiscal measures so that it can support the steady consumption

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and strengthening of business sentiment moving forward.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: If you look at the policy environment right now,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we are indeed in a very challenging external environment.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And the BSP will remain data dependent.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And is prepared to take further monetary policy actions

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to ensure that inflation returns to the 3% target over the medium term.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: So where do we see inflation moving forward?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Here, Mr. Chair, we showed the forecast, the outlook for inflation,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that we did in the last policy meeting back in June 18 of this year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this outlook will be updated this afternoon.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But just for recall, what we are seeing back in the last policy meeting

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: is that for 2026, inflation could average 6.4% this year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: So it could take a little bit of time before we see inflation going back again

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: or averaging again close to the target of 3%.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: At the same time, we emphasize another measure of inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this is what we call the core inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Core inflation is a measure of the underlying price pressure.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And it is something that is more lasting, more stable

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: in affecting the price dynamics in the economy.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this is something that we also closely monitor.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: What are some of the upside risks that we are looking at?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: There are several risks, and they could emanate from the higher

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: or elevated global oil prices, this anchoring of inflation expectations,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: as well as some impact, especially in the near term,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Now, if you look at the private sector surveys on their inflation forecast,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to higher inflation over the near term.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But their expectation is that inflation could indeed come back

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to close to the target by 2028.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Now, going to the banking system, how is the banking system performing?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The Philippine banking system remains healthy and supported by strong fundamentals.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In our oversight in supervising the banking sector,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we emphasize risk-based, forward-looking, and systemic risk-focused bank supervision.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This is important so that we can help ensure that banks sustain their growth in assets

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and deposits, as well as continued profitability.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Looking across different metrics, for example, those on capital adequacy, on liquidity,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: they all remain well above international norms.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: If you look at non-performing loans, they also continue to be manageable,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and the banks are well provisioned against this non-performing portion of their loan book.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Looking ahead, we think that the banking system is well positioned to support economic activity

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: An important element of the financial system is to provide efficient services

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And from an economic perspective, we want to ensure we can support the değilism of both

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And here we show some of the developments in terms of access to financial services.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The chart on the left shows the digital payments reach almost 65% of retail transactions

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This surpasses the targets of 50% up to 54%

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: What this highlights is that there's a continued momentum in the adoption of electronic payment channels in the country.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But again, there's also an important element into this growing digital payment system in our economy.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this refers to what are called network externalities.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This means that the value and convenience of our domestic payment system, our domestic electronic payment channels, increases as more consumers, more merchants, and more financial institutions participate in this financial ecosystem.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this is something that the BSP has been promoting.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: On the right side, we show the increasing number of bank deposit accounts.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: It has reached over 28 million accounts as of March 2026, with more than 170 banks offering basic deposit accounts.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: These are no-frills deposit accounts, and it would help financial inclusion in our country.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This is an important priority of the BSP.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We also welcome the recent announcements of several banks to reduce or waive interbank digital transaction fees.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This makes it more affordable and accessible for Filipino households.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: well as small businesses to access convenience of electronic fund

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: transfers. We also thank our legislators for the passage of an important law and

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we refer here to the anti-financial account scamming up. This is indeed a

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: vital legislation to continue to improve consumer protection to do stronger

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: safeguards for fraud and faster complaint resolution. This is important

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: support as we try to grow, expand our financial system, not only to the

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: traditional banks, but also through banks via the digital economy. Now moving to

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the external sector, we see that the external sector continue to provide some

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: protection from the effects of volatile external environment.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Our balance of payments, this is the total transactions of the Philippines

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: with the rest of the world, is in a deficit.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And an important component of that total balance of payments

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: is what we call the current account.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The current account captures the trade in goods as well as the trade in services.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: That is also in deficit, but it has narrowed last year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Now, for this year and 2027, next year,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the current account deficit is projected to slightly widen.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And this is something that we are monitoring.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But at the same time, we have observed that emerging markets

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that continue to push for investment-led growth

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: usually experience such a deficit in their current account.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Now, how is this deficit being supported right now?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And here we point to very important structural flows,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the OFW remittances, the receipts from our BPO industry,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to some extent, tourism receipts, as well as foreign direct investments.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: So these important inflows are vital to make sure that our external position

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: remains manageable and sustainable over time.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We also highlight that we maintain some buffers regarding our external,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and this is in terms of international reserves.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We show in the slide, Mr. Chair,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the recent number for our international reserves

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: is about $103 billion as of last month.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: If you compare it, it can pay 6.7 months' worth of imports of goods and services.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: our obligations for the next 12 months.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: So overall, that is the general macroeconomic landscape

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that we are working with at this time.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The key assumptions behind the proposed national budget

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: for fiscal year 2027 are shown, Mr. Chair, in this slide.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In terms of inflation, our forecast points to still elevated inflation,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: but still above the inflation target of 3%.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In terms of oil prices, in recent months,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: they continue to remain volatile and uncertain.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And we think that moving forward,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: oil prices will reflect geopolitical developments,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: including those happening in the Middle East.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In terms of exchange rate, they will be capturing,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: but at the same time also reflecting possible domestic headwinds

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: or some improvements in domestic performance.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: this will be reflecting the country's fiscal balance,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: as well as the policy of continued consolidation

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In terms of the international interest rates,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that the U.S. Fed may maintain a relatively cautious policy stance moving forward

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: for the rest of the year and into the next year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Finally, our exports of goods will grow, but at a modest rate.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: It will be supported by firm global demand,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But there could be some challenges,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: especially in the increased global trade uncertainty.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Now, let me end, Mr. Chair, with some questions.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: First, in terms of inflation outlook,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we think that inflation could remain elevated over the near term,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and this will require measured action to anchor inflation expectations

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We also have a resilient banking system,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and these factors will be important in supporting domestic economy.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Moving forward, the BSP is prepared to take further monetary policy actions,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: if needed, to help achieve price stability,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: our main mandate of the BSP.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Price stability is our main contribution to promoting sustainable and durable growth.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Since Governor Remolona has to be excused because of the Monetary Board meeting,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Will any of the deputy governors

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: If there are senators, do we have any for Governor Remolona?

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: I have a couple of quick questions, probably three the most.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: My first question, sir, is, we may have

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: overlooked that one of the causes of inflation is the peso-dollar exchange rate.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: My question is, are we going to experience again the exchange rate below 60 pesos to

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: a dollar or ever, or it will continue to go up?

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Because right now it's 61 plus, 61.72, the exchange rate today.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Because I was looking at my records, sir.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: It says like, causes of inflation, because the rising cost of important goods, oil, food,

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: raw materials, food, particularly fertilizers that we import, we depend so much on imported

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: It's true that when the goods are imported, when the peso goes down, the price of those

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: What we're doing, because we've learned that, if the peso weakens very sharply, the impact

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: of the exchange rate on inflation will be higher.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Pero kung mabagal ang galaw, hindi masyadong tinatamaan yung inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, what we do is to manage the sharp movements in the exchange rate.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: The exchange rate itself is something very hard to fix for a country like the Philippines.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: As you know, Senator, we've had a trade deficit that's about 13% of our GDP.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Kulang na kulang ang exports natin.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So mahirap yatang pigilin yung pagbaba ng peso.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Pwedeng pigilin para bumagal pero hindi kayang pigilin, hindi kayang i-fix, hindi kayang 60 pesos. Ganun lang.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Pero kung mabagal, hindi naman masyadong inflationary.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: But hopefully, our exports will grow.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: That's our challenge here in the exchange rate.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: I just have one follow-up question on that.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: How do we go around this?

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: If we can't do anything about the exchange rate, because we depend so much right now

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: on the remittances of our OFWs, and we thank God that they are there.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: So, other than remittances, sabi niyo, hindi rin po puwede yung exports dahil napakabagal.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Isa sa mga sakit ng ulo ng Bureau of Customs right now, ang daming pumapasok po na container imports.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Pero pag-export, natatambak ngayon diyan sa pier, sa mga kung saan-saan, masakit na po ang ulo ng commissioner natin.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: how to dispose those empty containers.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: So, anong nakikita ninyo in your studies?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Now, we can do something about it.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Gumawa tayong paraan na palakasin ang exports.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, for example, Pax Silica, it could help with exports.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: And Luzon Economic Corridor, it could help with exports.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: But it may take some time before we can do it.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Ang isa pang consideration dyan, Senator, yung savings rate natin.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Kasi pag binilang mo yung remittances at saka yung BPO, ang diperensya ng pumapasok na pera at saka lumalabas, ang tawag dun current account.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: ang current account natin, matagal nang negative.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: As much as possible, I hope our savings will increase.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: It's a bit difficult to say this, Senator.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Because we spend so much higher than what we make.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: You know, you only spend how much you make.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: But we spend more than what we make.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: The father and the mother have a salary of 50,000.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: And for the country as a whole, to finance it, it's a bigger investment than savings.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So to finance it, we'll borrow from abroad.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: That's all for me, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Yes, next is Senator Lacson, then Senator Hontiveros.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Last time we met, last year, di ba?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So once a year lang tayo nakikita, samantalahin ko na lang tanungin.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Tama po ba yung aking understanding na ang easing ng inflation ay nakabasis sa assumption na bumaba ba yung prices ng oil at saka sundan ko yung kay Senator Tulfo, yung stable yung exchange rate natin.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So ang tanong ko po, dahil nagbukas yung, kasi nakita ko yung graph ng inflation sa presentation,

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Nagbukas po yung Strait of Hormus June this year.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Kasi nga nagkaroon ng memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran na buksan. Pero temporary lang dahil August, hindi naman fully open, hindi naman fully closed pero nagsara uli.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So ang tanong ko po, paano natin matatarget yung inflation, yung movement kung beyond the government control,

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Yung mga factors o yung drivers like yung oil prices, exchange rate, ano po yung ating gagawing measures kasi hindi natin abot yun eh. Wala tayong kontrol eh.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So, at our end, ano po yung pwede lang natin gawin para masustain natin yung inflation rate?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Talagang wala tayong magagawa sa price of oil.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: At saka yung share natin sa demand for oil, 4% lang.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, kahit anong gawin natin, hindi natin mababago yun.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Yung price of oil, tinatamaan naman yung fertilizer.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Dahil yung fertilizer natin galing din sa oil.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So tatamaan yung presyo ng pagkain, presyo ng bigas.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So ang tinitira namin yung second round effects.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Kasi yung second round effects kaya nating—

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Demand side yung second round effects.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Halimbawa, yung presyo ng services, restaurants, yung mga ganoon.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Kaya nating pahinayin yung inflation doon.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Pero over time, mapapababa naman natin.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: For my education lang po, can we be more specific kung ano yung mga measures?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, ang strategy namin dahil ang number one tool na namin, yung interest rate.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, pag tumaas ang interest rate, mapapababa natin yung demand ng mga services,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: o yung mga tinatawag natin na second round effects ng mga items.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: How much po ang influence nung ating kayang gawin?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Inaabot tayo ng two years bago natin mabalik sa 3%.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you, Senator Lacson, Senator Hontiveros.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: At magandang umaga po muli, Gov.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Hindi lang naman po yung Pilipinas pero yung buong mundo ay naapektohan ng mga global headwinds. Pero bakit ang taas ng inflation figures natin kumpara sa mga kapitbahay natin, sa atin 6.2%, samantala ang Vietnam 4.4%, ang Thailand 1.95% at ang Malaysia 1.8%.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So ano po yung nag-a-account para sa diferensyang iyon na ang samanong epekto po sa atin?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Tayo yung napuruhan ng oil prices eh. Yung gaya ng Indonesia, merong oil sila although nag-iimport pa rin pero meron silang oil.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Malaysia, ganun din, may oil sila pero nag-iimport sila ng konti. So tayo, wala tayong oil talaga eh. So malakas ang tama talaga sa atin.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Tapos, just to oversimplify, Senator, pwede mong hatiin yung mga economists,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Yung may oil at saka yung walang oil. Wala tayong oil. Pwede nyo rin hatiin yung mga economists. Yung may AI at saka walang AI.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Tayo, wala tayong AI eh. Na totoong AI. So yung merong AI na mga economists, nakakompensate yung kanilang AI sector sa pagkakulangan ng oil.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So tayo, talo talaga tayo dun sa ganun mga aspects.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Although this is two oversimplified things.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Kahit sabi nyo po gov oversimplification, so dalawang factors, the haves and the have-nots, langis at saka AI, could you possibly give a third para may indication din po kami,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: kahit sa pag-examine ng anong dapat na budget para sa 2027 na adjustan po namin para masuportahan din yung mga measures na ginagawa nyo sa Banko Sentral

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: na i-tame at i-control ang inflation at ibalik siya.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So talaga dun sa trajectory papunta sa inflation target kahit by year 2028 pa.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So itong dalawa po ang dalawang pinaka-obvious na may posibleng positive effect sa pag-tame ng inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Salamat po, Governor. Salamat po, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you, Senator Ontiberos. Next is Senator Pangilinan.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Thank you, Magandang Maga, Governor, Deputy Governor.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Si Deputy Governor Abinoha and I sat in the NFA Council when I was Chairman and you were representing the BSP.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Food inflation actually is a driver of nationwide inflation.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: In fact, to be specific, rice inflation.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Rice inflation is a big driver, either driving it up or driving it down.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Would you consider that, Governor, one of the interventions that needs immediate addressing so that we can bring down nationwide inflation?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: I say this because, and I think Deputy Governor Abinoha will remember or perhaps you will recall,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: during our watch with the NFA having the...

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: powers that it used to have,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: we were able to flood NCR with up to 75% additional rice at that height when rice inflation was 15%

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: in June of 2014 when I first stepped in as Food Security Secretary.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: So much so that within one year,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: should not that be one major consideration for our

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: How do we manage, bring down, food inflation, particularly rice inflation?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: For the lower 30% of our household, food is 50% of their basket.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Ang rice kasi, ang tawag namin din, salient price.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: ng mga tao, yung presyo ng bigas,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Pag tumaas yung presyo ng bigas, may effects sa expectations.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Yung expectations, ano yan eh, part of the mechanism for inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, maganda kung hindi tumaas masyado yung presyo ng bigas.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Ang makakabuti, hindi po yung lalagyan natin ng cap, hindi masyado nakakatulong yung cap.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Ang mas mabuti, hindi po yung lalagyan natin ng cap, hindi masyado nakakatulong yung cap.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Ang mas mabuti, mataas natin, itaas natin yung productivity ng ating agriculture para mas malaki ang production natin ng rice.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Unfortunately, in terms of agri-exports, we continue to be a net importer instead of a net exporter.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: And we're doing very, not naman negligible, but nakakalungkot kung inkumpara yung ating agri-export.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: We're doing agri-exports sa Thailand, Indonesia.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: They're doing almost 60 plus billion dollars worth of agri-exports while we're doing about nine.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: So clearly, something is not right with precisely why food inflation,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: why nationwide inflation is high because food inflation is high.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Food inflation is high because productivity is low, supply is low.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: And therefore, when demand is high and supply is low, then prices will obviously go up.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: So it's actually a very basic, simple problem.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: I mean, simply defined, articulated problem.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Now, the challenge is how do you bring down food prices?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: I mean, that's really now up to the executive department through the DA.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: But you will agree that if we address food inflation by providing the right supply,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: we will bring down nationwide inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Next to ask question is, before we continue,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I'd like to, the chair would like to acknowledge the presence of Senator Robin Hood-Badilla.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Yes, just one quick question, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: In 2025, Governor Mo Lona, the president's budget inflation in the medium term

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: is supposed to stabilize at 2.2 to 4 percent from 2025 to 2028 with monetary policy.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: That's what was our advisors, the economic advisors were telling.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: This year, however, we adjusted the inflation assumption to 4 percent to 5 percent.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Well, whatever happened, what we're saying, stabilize at 2 to 4 percent,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: there are monetary policy and government interventions.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: So, our solution is to go up.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: We'll bring up our inflation to another 4 to 5 percent.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: As you know, Senator, the world has changed.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: In April, suddenly, there was a war.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: The oil prices went up more than ever before.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: More than during the start of the Ukraine invasion.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, if the situation has changed, the assumptions must be adjusted

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: But my question, sir, is, do we have any measures?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Like, don't we expect shocks like this?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Whatever happened, if there's this, if there's a catastrophe,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: the supply like this, we should have learned our lesson from last year

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: What if there's a severe drought that we'll experience or we cannot import

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: anymore from other countries because there's war?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Is this not factored in when you guys talk about inflation?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: What do we do if this will happen?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Do we have any measures, counter measures to avoid this?

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: To prepare our government, to prepare our people just in case we have Plan A,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: then we go to Plan B if this Plan A won't work.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: What we've done on our side, which is what we can do,

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: is to change the way we analyze inflation.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: If this happens, what is inflation?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: If this happens, what is inflation?

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: So, our scenario analysis is more serious now.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: This is after what happened here in Iran-US war.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: Because before, you don't have alternatives if situations arises

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: like what happened in the war in Iran.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: I just recall the question that I'd like to get from the point of view of the BSP.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: You know, the rice tarification measure when it was passed

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: was supposed to bring down rice prices.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: jumped from about 2 million metric tons a year,

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: it's now about 5 million metric tons a year.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
segments.text: And yet, the dent in rice prices is negligible.

segments.speaker: Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan
