DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the Philippines has also moved closer to its ASEAN peers through significant income gains.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Although significant income gains remain, reaching upper middle income status is an important achievement.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: But it's not the end in itself.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The greater challenge is to translate progress into better jobs, higher incomes, and improve living standards for Filipinos.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: To do so, we must first understand the factors behind the recent loss of economic momentum.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This slowdown largely reflected weaker domestic demand, as governance and corruption concerns,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and the Middle East conflict weighed on consumer and business confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Domestic demand grew by only 1.5% in the first half of 2026,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: down from 5.7% in the same period the previous year.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Investment contracted 6.5%, driven by a sharp decline in public construction.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Household consumption growth also eased to 2.9% amid elevated inflation and weaker confidence

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Exports provided some support, growing by 10%

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: On the production side, however, services remained the principal source of growth

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: while industry, contracted, and agriculture made only a modest contribution

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The slowdown in economic activity has also begun to affect the labor market.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The post-pandemic expansion created 4 million net jobs between the first half of 2022 and the first half of 2026,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: demonstrating how economic growth can create opportunities and improve livelihoods.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: However, as growth slowed, total employment declined by 166,000 over the past year.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The unemployment rate also rose to 4.2% in June 2026, up from 3.1% a year earlier.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These recent developments underscore the urgency of restoring economic momentum and generating more and better quality jobs.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Nonetheless, even with the recent slowdown, the longer-run benefits of

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: economic growth extended beyond employment to include poverty reduction. Poverty declined substantially, regardless of the poverty

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: threshold or norm applied. As income growth outpaced inflation, and gains were broadly shared

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Based on the country's official poverty lines and preliminary estimates for 2025,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: or not preliminary estimates, they are already official estimates,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: poverty incidence among Filipinos fell from 15.5% in 2023 to 9.7% in 2025.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This means that 6.5 million Filipinos were lifted out of poverty over this period.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This reflects the recovery of incomes and employment

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: as well as sustained implementation of social protection programs.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: However, these hard-earned gains remain vulnerable,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: largely driven by the impact of the Middle East conflict

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: on global oil and commodity prices.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: but it remains well above the government's target range.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: High inflation erodes household purchasing power,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The burden is even heavier when food prices rise faster

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: than non-food prices, because food accounts for a much larger share

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: among low-income families than among high-income families.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: it could slow or even reverse our recent advances

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Protecting our progress goes beyond addressing

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the immediate concerns of slower growth

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Protecting our progress goes beyond addressing the immediate concerns

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: of slower growth and elevated inflation.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: constraints that continue to limit the economy's productive capacity and resilience.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Let me now turn to these constraints, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: A central structural challenge is the economy's heavy reliance on household consumption on

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the demand side and on the services side of our economy and the production side.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Consumption remains the primary driver of economic growth, while contributions of fixed

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: investment and net exports have been modest.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Similarly, services account for most of the expansion, while agriculture and industry

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This experience of successful economies shows that sustained progress requires mobilizing

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: We must therefore broaden our growth pillars by strengthening investments and exports while

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The urgency of this task is evident from our performance relative to our ASEAN peers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: As the chart shows, Philippines continues to trail several neighboring economies in

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Despite improvement in recent years, investment expands productive capacity, facilitates the

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: adoption of new technologies, and creates better jobs.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Exports enable domestic firms to access larger markets, achieve economies of scale, and become

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Mobilizing greater investments and improving export competitiveness will depend critically

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The Government has substantially increased productive infrastructure spending in recent

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: years, yet this higher level of expenditure has not fully translated into stronger infrastructure

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This gap shows that the level of spending alone is not enough.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: We must also improve project selection, appraisal, procurement, implementation,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that public resources deliver high-quality infrastructure

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: on time and at reasonable cost.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Closing our infrastructure gaps will reduce production and logistics costs,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: connect people and markets, attract private investment,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: faster growth also requires greater innovation and stronger productivity.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The Philippines, Mr. Chair, has made encouraging progress in innovation

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: as reflected in its improved ranking in the Global Innovation Index.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: However, this has yet to translate into stronger overall productivity,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the efficiency with which the economy uses its resources to produce goods and services.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: As the chart on the right shows,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: performance remains weak relative to several of our regional peers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Innovation contributes to development only when new knowledge and technologies

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: are widely adopted by firms, farms, and workers,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and when they are translated into more efficient production,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: better products, and higher value activities.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: We must therefore strengthen the connection among research,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The weaknesses we have discussed do not stem from a single source.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: They reflect persistent and interconnected constraints across markets and institutions

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that continue to hinder investment, productivity, and diversification.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Addressing them requires coordinated action by government,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: in close coordination with Congress, the private sector, and other stakeholders.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This brings us to our growth targets and priorities for advancing the economy.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Our direction remains anchored in the Philippine Development Plan.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Over the Administration's final two years, the focus is on accelerating execution,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: resolving implementation bottlenecks, and translating reforms into concrete results.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Given the slowdown in recent quarters, economic growth is projected to be at 3.5% to 4.5% in 2026.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: With faster implementation of public programs and infrastructure projects, improved domestic supply conditions, and restored consumer and investor confidence, growth is expected to recover to 5% to 6% over the next two years.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Inflation is expected to remain elevated in 2026, as already shown earlier by the BSP.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Ease to 4% to 5% in 2027, and return to the government's 2% to 4% target range by 2028.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Meanwhile, employment conditions are expected to improve as the economy recovers, keeping unemployment within the government's target range.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These targets are attainable, but they remain subject to significant domestic and external risks.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Foremost among the domestic risks are further delays in the execution of public investments, leading to continued underspending, as well as continuing governance concerns that could further weaken consumer and investor confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Severe weather disturbances could also constrain food production, and intensify inflationary pressure.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Externally, the prolonged Middle East conflict could keep global oil and commodity prices elevated, while geopolitical and trade tensions may weaken global demand and disrupt supply chains.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: To manage this risk, we have established clear imperatives.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: protect vulnerable households, accelerate public investments, and restore confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: First, we will protect poor and low-income families against high food prices

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and supply disruptions through targeted and timely assistance,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: while strengthening the domestic food supply and maintaining adequate buffers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Second, implementing agencies will accelerate high-impact infrastructure projects

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: through catch-up plans with clear milestones and accountability measures.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This is essential to reverse underspending and restore public investment as a driver of growth.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Third, we need to address governance and corruption concerns

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: improving monitoring, and ensuring the efficient use of public resources.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: limited public resources must be directed toward high-impact, implementation-ready investments.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Priorities include addressing learning poverty and classroom shortages,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: strengthening primary health care, particularly in underserved areas,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: raising farm productivity through climate-resilient technologies and post-harvest infrastructure,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and accelerating transport, logistics, energy, and digital infrastructure

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: through the Build Better, More program and public-private partnerships.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These investments must be pursued while safeguarding fiscal sustainability.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This requires stronger coordination across planning, investment programming, budgeting,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and execution of infrastructure and social programs.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: We also need to improve spending efficiency,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and revenue measures that do not erode the government's fiscal position.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Looking ahead, sustained structural reforms will be needed to raise productivity,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: strengthen competitiveness, and expand the economy's long-term growth potential.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Key priorities include ensuring more reliable and affordable energy,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: by expanding renewable generation, modernizing the power grid,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and streamlining the net metering and permitting processes,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and strengthening competition in the electricity market.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Domestic production and external competitiveness must likewise be strengthened

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: by moving into higher value segments of global value chains,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: sustaining the country's advantages or advantage in services,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and expanding market access for Philippine exports.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Deeper financial and capital markets will also be essential

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to mobilize long-term financing for infrastructure and productive enterprises.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Legislation will be indispensable to advance advancing this reform agenda.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The priority measures fall into four broad areas.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Governance and anti-corruption reforms include measures addressing political dynasties, the party-led system, freedom of information, bank secrecy, and public budgeting.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Economic growth and resilience measures include tax reforms and amendments affecting the coconut and fisheries sector.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Energy priorities include amendments to EPIRA and waste-to-energy legislation.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Measures in education, health, and social protection aim to improve nutrition, accelerate classroom construction, expand access to education, and strengthen assistance to vulnerable Filipinos.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Again, Congress' continued partnership will be critical to advancing these reforms.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: growth, and improving the lives of Filipinos.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: As we enter the final years of the administration, our objective is to turn reforms into results.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This means accelerating the implementation of high-impact programs and projects, the surest path to recovering growth, extending its benefits to more Filipinos, and building an economy resilient enough to withstand future shocks.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: None of this can be achieved by any agency alone.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: It requires efficient and coordinated action across the entire government.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: We look forward to our continued partnership with this committee as we work to deliver stronger, broader, and more inclusive growth in the years ahead.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: More importantly, we have maintained a prudent debt mix,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: First, 67% of our outstanding debt is domestic.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: This reduces our exposure to foreign exchange risks,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: while also supporting the continued development of our local capital market.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: This has been the direction since the start of this administration.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Second, 90% of our debt carries fixed interest rates.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: This provides greater certainty in our debt servicing costs

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and shields us from sudden increases or fluctuations in global interest rates.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And third, 84.1% of our debt has long-term repayment periods,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: meaning we have several years before these obligations fall due.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: This strategic borrowing mix by our Bureau of Treasury

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: strengthens our resilience to external shocks

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and makes our debt obligations more predictable and manageable over the long term.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: while helping broaden our investor base,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: maintain access to key international markets,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and support the continued development of our local bond market.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: With tax collections projected to grow by an average of 9% annually from 2026 to 2028,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: total revenues are targeted to reach 5.5 trillion pesos by the end of the President's term.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: This means our revenue agencies will have to raise the bar even further.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The BIR and BOC will need to continue improving efficiency,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and leveraging technology to sustain faster growth in collections.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: we are looking to pursue reforms that will make our revenue systems more efficient,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We are promoting growth, revenue, and equity towards socio-economic sustainability or progress

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: through a comprehensive reform package that provides targeted tax relief

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We likewise expect more revenues from the proposed Multinational Minimum Tax Bill,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: which will preserve our taxing rights and ensure the taxes arising from economic activity in the Philippines

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And the General Tax Amnesty Bill mentioned by the President in his SONA

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to encourage the settlement of outstanding tax obligations,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and bring more taxpayers into the formal tax system.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Disbursements will grow moderately from 2026 to 2028.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We must be more deliberate where we put our resources.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Prioritize investments that strengthen our productive capacity,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and deliver tangible benefits to our people.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We must focus on programs and investments that

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: generate the greatest economic and social

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: returns, particularly in critical infrastructure, health, education, and other areas that support

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: long-term growth. As revenues grow faster than disbursements, we will see a clear and sustained

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: path towards fiscal consolidation. The deficit-to-GDP ratio is projected to steadily decline

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: from 5.4 percent in 2026 to 3.5 percent by 2030, putting us on a progressively stronger fiscal

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: footing. This improving fiscal trajectory is also reflected in our debt outlook. From 2026 to 2030,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: both national government and general government debt ratios are projected to decrease.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: NG debt is projected to ease from 65 percent to 63 percent in 2030,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and general government debt is expected to decline from 59 percent to 56 percent by 2030.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: As we look ahead, the path we had laid out is clear. We assure the honorable members of this

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: chamber that the economic team will continue to strengthen revenues, manage expenditures

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: responsibly, reduce the deficit, and keep our debt on a sustainable path. At the same time,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: we are building fiscal buffers that will give us room to respond to future shocks without compromising our long-term fiscal sustainability.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We look forward to working closely with the Senate to ensure that the government lives within its

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: means. This means making difficult choices, prioritizing programs and investments with

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the greatest impact, and ensuring that new spending commitments are matched by sustainable

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: sources of funding. Fiscal discipline is not just about reducing the deficit.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: More important is that we engage in smart spending. Our national budget can work harder

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: if we invest in programs and projects that can help shape our future. The government must continue

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to address the immediate needs of our people, but we must look beyond the present and invest in high

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: multiplier programs and projects that create lasting economic value, those that create jobs,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: raise incomes, and build a stronger economy tomorrow.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Well-chosen infrastructure, for example, does more than address today's needs. It can generate

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: economic activity, connect communities, attract private investment, and deliver benefits for many

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: years to come. Let us work together to make the 2027 national budget count and ensure that its

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: benefits ripple through generations. This is the fiscal discipline we owe to the Filipino people. Maraming salamat po.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Next is Acting Secretary Kim De Leon. But how long is your presentation, Secretary De Leon?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: 27 slides, maybe another 20 minutes. So if there's pressure, maybe, probably, we can go on the quick lunch break first.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: You can go ahead, and then we'll just have the lunch.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chair. To Senate President Win Gatchalian, Senate Finance Committee Chair J.V. Ejercito,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Honorable Members of the Senate Finance Committee and the Senate, my fellow economic managers and colleagues in government,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: good morning. As Acting Secretary of the DBM and Chair of the DBCC, it is my honor to present to the Senate of the Philippines

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: of the fiscal year 2027 national expenditure program.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: For fiscal year 2027, we are proposing a

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: of our country's gross domestic product.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This budget is 47 billion pesos or 6%

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: higher than the fiscal year 2026 GAA. Much of this increase is already accounted for

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: by mandatory expenditures and existing fiscal commitments by the government.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This includes higher national tax allotments for our local government units,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the fourth tranche of the salary adjustment for civilian government employees under EO64,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the corresponding salary increases for our military and uniformed personnel,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and other obligations that the government must honor.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We would like to highlight that the 6% increase in the overall budget

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: should not be interpreted to mean a uniform increase across agencies and programs.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because limited fiscal space demands disciplined choices,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we prioritize programs and projects that are implementation-ready,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: capable of delivering the greatest impact and offer the best value for every Filipino.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The P7.2 trillion budget before us, therefore, represents more than a spending ceiling.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: It is the product of months of rigorous review to ensure that we will

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: meet the country's most urgent needs today, without compromising our capacity to meet the challenges of tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The fiscal year 2027 national budget carries the theme

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: People-Centered Growth for an Inclusive and Resilient Future,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: effectively capturing a simple but critical principle.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Economic progress must ultimately be measured by how it improves the lives of Filipinos.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We want growth that reaches communities,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: creates opportunities across sectors and regions,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But crafting a budget that would translate

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: this vision into reality requires more than

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: When government agencies submitted more than

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: P11 trillion in budget proposals for possible inclusion in the NEP

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we could not simply ask how much

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: questions such as which programs are

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: ready to deliver, which will make the

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: every peso generate the greatest value

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: These questions shaped the decisions behind this budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the President's direction was clear. Public resources must translate into

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: real and meaningful benefits for Filipinos across every region and community, through to the spirit

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: of our vision of Bawat Bayan Makikinabang. Beyond funding requirements, we also look closely at how

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: agencies have utilized the resources already entrusted to them. Their actual budget performance

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and implementation capacity were key considerations in determining their allocations under the fiscal

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: year 2027 national budget. As of June 30, 2026, total available appropriations stood at 7.54 trillion

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Of this amount, 6.63 trillion pesos had been released as allotments to various agencies,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: including 546.79 billion pesos from continuing fiscal year 2025 appropriations.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Agencies had obligated 3.29 trillion pesos, or about 49.5 percent, of released allotments,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: comprising of 3.13 trillion from the current year appropriations and the remaining 158.58

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: billion from the current year appropriations.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Of the obligations reported, 81.9 percent had already been disbursed.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: As of the same period, June 30, 2026, unreleased appropriations among

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: amounted to 820.21 billion from the current-year GAA and 89.7 billion from the 2025 continuing appropriations.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We would like to note that as of July 31, 2026, the DBM has released a total allotment of 6.18 trillion, equivalent to 91% of the program, leaving a balance of 610.95 billion pesos.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Of the 4.39 trillion program under the 2026 GAA, total allotments issued reached 3.85 trillion with a remaining balance of 537.32 billion pesos.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This balance includes 315.9 billion pertaining to agency-specific budgets and 221.41 billion under special purpose funds.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: These indicators help us assess whether additional resources can be used.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The DBM will continue working closely with the agencies to improve their execution of their budget because the true measure of a budget is not simply how much is approved or released, but how effectively these resources become real results for our people.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Now, allow me to provide updates on the national government's disbursements for fiscal years 2025 to 2025.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: NG disbursement in 2025 reached 6.03 trillion pesos, equivalent to 21.5% of GDP.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This was mainly driven by PS expenditures for salaries and benefits of government workforce such as education and health sectors, including the military and uniformed personnel.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: MOOE also contributed strongly to the government's spending performance, owing to the implementation of social protection programs, agricultural services, and the development of a new government.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: As well as the general operations of the government.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Meanwhile, disbursements are projected to increase by 7% on the average this year in 2027, reaching 6.466 trillion this year and 6.901 trillion next year.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Spending will continue to be supported by PS expenditures, reflective of the higher salaries of civilian government employees and higher base pay and subsistence allowance of MUPs.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: As well as the general operations of the government.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: As well as the requirements for creation and filling up of positions in various departments, particularly in education and health.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Both MOOE and infrastructure expenditures will remain significant to fund priority human capital development programs and flagship infrastructure projects, respectively.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The overall support to local government units will also continue to be substantial, driven by larger NTA shares, annual block grant to the BARM,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and annual financial support to the NTA.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The proposed financial assistance through the local government support fund.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Moving forward with the dimensions of the 2027 National Budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The proposed 2027 National Budget is composed of two main sources.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Programmed appropriations amount to 4.494 trillion pesos

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and will finance the priority programs, projects, and operations of government.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: expenditures already mandated by existing laws. Major automatic appropriations include 1.32

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: trillion peso for the national tax allotment of LGUs, 1.114 trillion pesos for interest payments,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: 104.2 billion pesos for the annual block grant of the BARM, and 89 billion pesos for the retirement

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and life insurance premiums of national government employees. This demonstrates that a considerable

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: portion of the 7.2 trillion peso budget is already determined by laws, formulas, and existing

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: obligations before government even begins deciding which new or expanded programs to fund.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We have likewise brought and programmed the appropriations down substantially to 112 billion

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: pesos. Nominally, this is the lowest proposed UA in the NEP since 2019, while its 1.56 percent

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: share is the lowest in the U.S.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: share of the total expenditure program is the lowest ratio since 1991. Allow me to reiterate

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: that unprogrammed appropriations are not automatically available for spending. It is a

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: standby spending authority for specifically identified purposes that may be accessed only

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: when the funding conditions prescribed by law are satisfied. For fiscal year 2027,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the unprogrammed appropriations have been deliberately limited primarily to

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: partially finance the restoration of the fund balance previously remitted by the PDIC and to

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: support foreign-assisted projects that are still undergoing assessment and evaluation by the

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Investment Coordination Committee and require approval by the ED Council. By keeping standby

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: appropriations to the minimum necessary, the administration is placing more expenditures

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: under programmed appropriations, thereby strengthening expenditure planning,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and ensuring the timely implementation of priority programs and projects. By expense class,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the proposed budget reflects our commitment to sustaining government operations while directing

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: resources toward investments with lasting economic and social returns. MOOE amounts to 2.944

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: trillion pesos. Notably, MOOE declines by 36.2 billion or 1.2 percent from 2026 level,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: as the total national budget increases by 6 percent. This indicates that the overall budget growth is not being driven by a broad expansion of operating expenditures.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: PS will receive 1.982 trillion up by 138.2 billion or 7.5 percent. This will support public servants who will deliver education,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: healthcare, public safety, national defense, and other essential services, while also providing for salary adjustments,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and personal requirements already committed by the government.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We would like to emphasize that both PS and MOOE remain fully covered by our projected revenues.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Meanwhile, capital outlays increased to 1.16 trillion pesos,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: an increase of 140.8 billion or 13.8% to finance infrastructure, facilities, equipment, and other productive assets.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Financial expenses amount to 1.114 trillion pesos, up by 164.3 billion or 17.3% largely due to interest payments.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Nevertheless, we affirm that our debt remains manageable as debt servicing is explicitly provided for in the budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Our approach is not to pursue deficit reduction at the expense of growth.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Instead, we are advancing a strategic and gradual fiscal consolidation path

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: that supports the development of a new economy.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This safeguards our obligations and fiscal credibility while preserving the investments needed to strengthen our people and sustain our economic growth.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Across the five sectors of the proposed budget, social services will continue to receive the largest share at 2.456 trillion or 34.1%.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This will directly support education, health, social protection, employment, housing, and other services that affect the everyday lives of people.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Economic services will receive 1.833 trillion or 25.5% for infrastructure, agriculture, transportation, water resources, digital connectivity, and other investments that improve productivity.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: General public services account for 1.317 trillion or 18.3%, while defense will receive 452.4 billion or 6.3%.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Debt burden accounts for 1.13 trillion or 15.9%, covering interest payments and net lending to government corporations.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Honoring these obligations protect the government's creditworthiness

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and helps preserve access to financing for future investments.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Our task is to maintain that balance, honoring our government's obligations

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: while continuing to fund what our people need.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: By recipient units, national government agencies will receive 4.332 trillion,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the largest share of the budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: However, their allocation grows by only 4.5%, below the overall budget growth of 6%,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: reflecting continued restraint in national government spending.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Local government units will receive 1.533 trillion, including a 1.32 trillion NTA,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This means roughly 129.3 billion more, or about 11%,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: will flow directly to LGUs to support devolved functions and frontline services.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: GOCCs will receive 220.5 billion, while 1.114 trillion will go to interest payments.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: These allocations underscore an important feature of the 2027 budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Resources are not concentrated solely at the national level,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: a substantial share is transferred to LGUs,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: bringing our country's resources closer to the communities

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: where many essential public services are delivered to our citizens.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The same principle is also evident in the regional distribution of the budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Of the proposed 7.2 trillion, 4.603 trillion, or 63.9%,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: is directly attributable to the regions.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The national capital region accounts for 1.112,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The remaining 2.597 trillion, or 36.1%, is non-regionalized,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: consisting of 1.983 trillion pesos in nationwide allocations

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and 613.8 billion in central office allocations.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the important distinction of nationwide from Metro Manila.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Nationwide allocations pertain to funds that are still to be distributed

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to various regions of the departments and agencies,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: as this cannot yet be geographically assigned at the time the NEP was prepared.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Ultimately, the majority of the budget is intended to reach our regions and communities.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: That is what we mean when we say,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and priorities of the budget established,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: let us now turn to where our most significant investments will be directed,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and how this will translate into better outcomes for Filipinos.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Education remains at the center of our investment in human capital.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The Department of Education will receive the highest allocation at 975.96 billion pesos,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: while 176.5 billion is provided for higher education

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Taken together with the other components of government education spending,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: our proposed investment in basic and higher education reaches 1.326 trillion,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: equivalent to nearly 4% of the GDP,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and effectively reaching the lower bound of the UNESCO Education 2030 benchmark

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: of 4-6% of GDP for education spending for the second time.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The difference between the two is that, for the first time,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: between 1.314 trillion reflected in the President's budget and the 1.326 trillion presented during the DBCC briefing at the House

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: is due to the inclusion of the Tier 2 projections for BARM education agencies which were not yet available when the budget message was prepared and printed.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: By the time of the House briefing, these projections were already available and were therefore included in computing the overall education sector figure.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So, to be clear, there was no change in the 2027 NEP after its submission.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The difference simply reflects the more complete BARM education sector figures,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: which is available at the time of the DBCC presentation.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This is consistent with how we view education as a national commitment,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: one that leaves no learner behind, whether served by our national education agencies, in BARM, and in all communities across the country.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: these allocations translate into specific investments.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We are proposing 12.09 billion for the expanded career progression system for public school teachers,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: an increase of almost 6 billion or 96.6% from the current year.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This is to support the reclassification and career advancement of our teachers.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Another 10.36 billion allocation next year will also sustain the 10,000 peso teaching allowance under the Kabalika,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: 61.1 billion is provided for the universal access to quality tertiary education across state universities and colleges,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: supporting free higher education, tertiary education subsidies,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the significance of the 1.326 trillion peso budget

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: will not be measured by the amount of education.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This is to support the development of the education sector,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and to support the development of the education sector.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: It will be measured by better learning outcomes, better supported teachers, wider access to education and training, and more opportunities for Filipino learners to build a future they rightfully deserve.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The top 10 departments with the largest allocations account for 51.4% of the proposed budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Apart from education, major allocations will go to public works and highways, health, interior and local government, national defense, transportation, agriculture, social welfare and development, higher education, and the judiciary, fully aligned with the administration's priorities and the Philippine development.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: On infrastructure, let me emphasize that infrastructure is more than just the DPWH budget. Under the Build Better More infrastructure program, the government is proposing 1.467 trillion pesos, equivalent to 4.4% of GDP for infrastructure in 2027.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: These investments are distributed across public works, transportation, agriculture, education, defense, health, digital infrastructure, and other sectors.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Specifically, DPWH will receive 643.95 billion, or the second largest allocation among agencies.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This is partly to support ongoing locally funded and foreign-assisted infrastructure flagship projects.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Major projects include the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network Project at 35 billion, Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge Project at 22 billion, Davao City Bypass Construction Project Package 1 at 11.9 billion,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Cebu-Mactan Bridge and Coastal Road Construction Project at 8.5 billion, and Pasig-Marikina River Channel Improvement Project Phase 4 at 8.5 billion pesos.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Transportation is likewise a major priority.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: With 300.96 billion proposed for the DOTR and its attached agencies.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This includes 123.84 billion for the North-South Commuter Railway System, 67.44 billion for Phase 1 of the Metro Manila Subway Project, and 1.94 billion for the MRT Line 3 Rehabilitation Project.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: 175.49 million is provided for the Cebu Bus Rapid Transit Project, and 15.08 billion for the Davao Public Transport Modernization Project.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We are also investing 8.99 billion in the new Cebu International Container Port Project, and 1.41 billion in the new Dumaguete Airport Development Project.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: These investments demonstrate that reducing travel time and logistics costs, connecting regional economies,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: improving the movement of people and goods, and bringing more Filipinos within reach of jobs and economic opportunities are important priorities of this administration.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Our other major investments pursue the same objective of improving people's security and quality of life.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Across the agriculture sector, 261.7 billion will support food security, productivity, and the livelihood.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The proposed fiscal year 2027 budget continues to make quality healthcare more accessible, more affordable, and more responsive to the needs of every Filipino by allocating 353.8 billion for the health sector.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We are providing 107.29 billion for the operations of DOH regional hospitals and other health facilities.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Along with 28.19 billion for DOH hospitals and Metro Manila to expand healthcare capacity, modernize facilities, and strengthen specialized medical services.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This means more Filipinos can access quality healthcare closer to home, while those requiring highly specialized treatment continue to receive world-class care in our major public hospitals.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: To further reduce what Filipino families,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: from out of their own pockets when they are hospitalized,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we are strengthening the implementation of the universal healthcare through PhilHealth

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: with an allocation of 74.45 billion pesos.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This will support the continued expansion of the PhilHealth's benefit packages,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: including the implementation of zero-balance billing in both DOH and LGU hospitals.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: From only six LGU hospitals this year,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: zero-balance billing will expand to 352 LGU hospitals nationwide next year,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: allowing millions more Filipinos to receive quality hospital care without worrying about the cost.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: More importantly, this means that when illness strikes,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Filipino families can focus on their loved ones' recovery,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: not on how they will pay the hospital bill.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This is our commitment to making quality healthcare more accessible,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: more affordable, and more compassionate to every Filipino.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: For social protection, DSWD will receive 241 billion,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: including 99 billion for the implementation of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: For national defense, 328.8 billion is proposed,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: including 50 billion for the revised AFP modernization program

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and 10 billion higher than the current year's level.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The Philippine Coast Guard will receive 45.51 billion,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: while 73.67 billion is proposed for the subsistence allowance

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: of our military and uniformed personnel across concerned agencies.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: For the judiciary, 86.27 billion is included

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to support the administration of justice and access to judicial services.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Consistent with the constitutional principle of judicial independence

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and the provisions of the Judiciary Fiscal Autonomy Act,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the Supreme Court's original budget proposal has been incorporated into the fiscal year 2027 NEP,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: recognizing the judiciary's fiscal autonomy and constitutional mandate.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Resilience is likewise integral to the 2027 budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: including 14.67 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program for LGUs and 1 billion for the People's Survival Fund.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Taken together, these investments reveal the broader purpose of the 2027 budget

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to protect vulnerable Filipinos, strengthen human capital and food security,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and improve our ability to withstand future shocks.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: That commitment extends directly to our local government units.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: 1.32 trillion NTA gives LGUs greater resources to perform devolved functions,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: while 115.62 billion will support peace, self-governance,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and long-term development in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We are likewise proposing 58.53 billion for the Local Government Support Fund,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: covering financial assistance to LGUs, the Growth Equity Fund, and the Barangay Development Program.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: By strengthening local fiscal capacity, we bring resources and decision-making closer to communities

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and give every region a stronger voice in national development.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: This is what people-centered growth means, one that reaches every community,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and ensures that progress is broadly and fairly shared across the country.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: These are only some of the key priorities reflected in the proposed Fiscal Year 2027 National Budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: To provide a broader view of the programs and projects we seek to pursue,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we have also prepared a short video presentation that we can probably share later.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Senate President, Mr. Chairperson, and Honorable Members of the Senate,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: before you represents the Executive's best judgment

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: of how limited public resources can respond to the country's immediate needs

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: while protecting our long-term fiscal and development goals.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But we also recognize that budget-making process does not end with the submission of the NEP.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The scrutiny of Congress is an essential part of that process.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The questions you will raise, the programs you examine,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and the choices we make together will ultimately,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We will determine whether the national budget is able to deliver what our people expect from government. On the part of the DBM and the Development Budget Coordination Committee, we come before the Senate prepared to explain our assumptions, account for our recommendations, and engage constructively throughout the deliberations.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because behind every number we discuss in this hearing is a consequence beyond these halls, a classroom that may be built, a hospital patient who may receive care, a farmer who may gain better access to markets, a community protected from disaster, or a Filipino family given a better opportunity to move forward.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: That is the standard by which this budget should ultimately be judged, not simply by how much government spends.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But by how much better government is able to serve.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We therefore look forward to working with the Senate toward a fiscal year 2027 national budget that is disciplined in its choices, credible in its commitments, transparent in its use, and meaningful in the lives of our people.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito

segments.text: And then the answer was, we are adapting.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: I want to point out that the Senate has a committee on sustainable development goals, innovation, and futures thinking.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: So in our capacity, during the budget, we chaired the...

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: that they have a futures thinking office.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: So maybe you can just give me a nod if you will want to consider that.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: These key agencies that I handled, that's why they have a budget for the futures thinking office.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: Because it just requires somebody trained in futures thinking

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: and who will be at a fairly high level so that they can participate in the discussions.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: And I want you to know in other countries, they have a system such that they are thinking of seven years hence.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: It's for the benefit of the entire economic team.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: Secretary De Leon, this is also important to you.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: There are countries that think of that.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: So it's not just for the next storm, it's not just for El Nino that will come in two months.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: That's how we have to plan.

segments.text: the Natural Gas Industry Development Act, which I sponsored and defended,

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.text: during the time of the former President Marcos, Sr.,

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
