segments.text: Ang tanong ko po, may we ask for further submission.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: List of LGUs highly subsidized or dependent to the national...

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: And then sa GOCC, bakit may decrease doon sa share ng GOCC?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, one of the primary reason for the decrease in the attributed allocation for GOCC,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So the biggest one is because of the one-time 60 billion that we return to PhilHealth under the 2026 GAA, Your Honor, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Yung babasa natin yung subsidy sa GOCC for the simple reason that there are so many non-performing GOCCs.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: And I want to find out from you, what is the new policy of the government?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Ito yung year in, year out, sinasubsidize yung national government.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Unlike the others na nakakakuha tayo from the GOCCs.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Pero yung iba naman, talagang persistently, no?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Walang income, lahat expenses, walang revenues, pero tuloy-tuloy naman yung subsidies.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Why don't we just abolish them?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Or not fund them, for that matter.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: If it's not abolished by law, kung hindi nyo ipa-fund, hindi rin makapangsyon, di ba?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, the supervision of the GOCCs are under the GCG.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And the GCG already has on its table currently about 21 GOCCs that they would like to close,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: wind down, or be absorbed by other...

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The truth of the matter, Your Honor, is that it's a very slow, long, and tedious process to shut down.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But there are currently 21 companies that we would like to shut down.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: How much is the total subsidy being provided by the government sa mga non-performing, yung mga negative na GOCCs?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: On the average, say, for the past...

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: From 2022 hanggang 2026, magkano na inaabon na ng national government?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Kasi nasa very tight ating fiscal space, di ba?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So it's about time that we discuss this and talk about this and implement.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, as for the amounts included in the 2027 NEP,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: most of the GOCCs where we provided subsidy are those performing critical social service functions.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But we will have to check as to the list, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, of the definition of non-performing and will gladly provide a listing on the subsidy included for those types of GOCCs.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Who may not be necessarily performing social service functions, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: And of course, I understand the complexities, kasi may mga madidisplaced na mga staff, mga personnel that are manning those GOCCs.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: In case we abolish them, ano yung contingency?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Para doon sa mga, of course, their government employees, ano yung contingency?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Maybe that's one of the reasons why you're finding difficulty in abolishing yung ibang GOCCs.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Pero we cannot also afford to consider humanitarian reasons in lieu of the very tight fiscal space that we're having now.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: being also an ex-officio member of the GCG along with the Secretary of Finance,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: when we discussed these matters at the Commission,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we have this consideration naman po of the separation incentive that might be offered for consideration of possible affected personnel.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: It's such that I agree with the Secretary of Finance that there is this tedious process that we have to undertake

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: before we can even submit a recommendation for any action.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Meaning abolition, merger, or any possible action for the GOCC.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Your Honor, Mr. Chair, if I may, now that I'm looking at the list of non-performing GOCCs as a sample,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: in fact, I'm very much aware of some of these GOCCs coming back to us when we submitted the NEP and was asking for more.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But the fundamental principle that we implemented when we finalized the level is that

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: if they are not actually performing social service functions,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the subsidy that we can provide is only limited to their bare operating requirements, meaning their PS.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because for their expansion, they should be able to earn for whatever they would like to spend for.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Okay, yung regionalized budget against the national.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: You know, I'm glad that the President issued the Exceded Order No. 82, diba?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: During the campaign, when he was joining us,

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: he used to visit the Regional Development Council meetings, or he used to join.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: But yung implementation, how is it being implemented now?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Because I remember during the past budget deliberations,

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: parang naglilinger lang doon sa hovering doon sa 20 to 30 percent lang

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Or the output of the Regional Development Councils, of course,

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: coming from the barangay, municipal, city, municipality, city, and even provincial.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: But pag nabuo na yung NEP, nasa mga 20, 25 percent lang yung share nila doon sa output nila.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So what's the use of the Regional Development Councils discussing their regional development plans

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: 25 percent lang pala yung maipapasok sa NEP.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So now I want to find out from you, Mr. Secretary,

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: ano yung ratio between yung truly representative of the regional development

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: doon sa central or sa national government?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Kasi nakalagay dito, regionalized budget, nasa mga 63.9 percent.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: ang nag-implement din dyan, national government, di ba?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Nakasulat lang dito, regionalized, but actually,

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: hindi naman ito yung nanggaling sa regional or output ng mga regional development councils.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Because who would know the needs and priorities of the local government units

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, we shared the sentiment,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: in terms of the amount of efforts being poured into by our RDCs in screening and examining the budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And I believe our colleagues from DepDev would also give us about 25 to 30 percent still as a figure.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And that's precisely why we are working together with DepDev to address this matter structurally and on a policy level.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because there appears to be a disconnect, Your Honor, Mr. Chair,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: not only in terms of the budget, but also in terms of the budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: In terms of the submission and endorsement of agency central offices when it comes to proposals.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Kasi po yung mga RDCs should be submitting their proposals to the agency central offices.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And in turn, ang mga agency central offices po yung magpapadala sa DBM nung level that they have endorsed.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So that's just one of the potential disconnect.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But the second is also the timing.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The timeline of the planning between national budgeting and the local planning process

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So these are the two things, Your Honor, Mr. Chair, that we are addressing with DepDev.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And we're exploring now, one, moving the timelines as well in terms of preparation and endorsement of all these projects.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And for our two systems to talk to one another to increase the batting average of RDC-endorsed projects

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: landing not even in the NEP, but even in the agency central office proposals themselves.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: I personally looked into this matter and asked for the same thing, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But the system right now and the calendar of the preparation of the RDC-endorsed budget

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and the national budget proposal seems to have some disconnect in terms of that submission, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Yeah. I'm glad you raised that point because ito yung perennial problem, lagi ko rin kinu-question.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Since time immemorial, dahil hindi nga in sync ang budget call ninyo.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Mr. Chairman, my time is up.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Pero last point na lang ito.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Para hindi ma-skip sa mind ko.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Yung budget call nyo, nag-start ito mga sometime in February or March.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Pero yung DBCC, yung ano, I mean the Regional Development Councils, parang natatapos sila, what, October, November?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Same year, for the same budget year?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Why don't we synchronize na yung for the succeeding budget year, mauna yung RDC para makonsolidate and spare us, you know, spare us legislators from folders being carried by local government officials down to barangay officials?

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Yan ang problema namin ngayon. Mag-i-start na yan.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Puno yung hallway namin kasi nga nakaligtaan yung kanilang hindi nadala sa NEP.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So you can, you know, you can spare us from the problems of, you know, facing these local government officials knocking at our doors.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Ako walang problema. Hindi ako pinupuntaan. Alhamdulillah, wala akong, well, wala na yung pork barrel anyway.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So kindly synchronize yung mabuti na andyan ka na, Secretary Kim, kasi ito rin yung lagi naming nire-raise sa previous DBM secretaries, pero hindi na-implement.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: So with that, thank you, Mr. Chairman.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you, Senator Lacson. Please, President.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, that's definitely something we're working out with DEP-DEV.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: One is synchronizing the calendar and two, institutionalizing the same through the Philippine Budgeting Code that we are also advocating.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And in the Senate, it's very much supported by the Senate and led by the good Senate President.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: That includes the vertical alignment in terms of planning and budgeting linkage.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Yes, Mr. Chairman. I was listening attentively to the questions raised by Senator Lacson and we encountered yung mga non-performing GOCCs, Mr. President,

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: I mean, GOCCs, Mr. President, and that's part of what I'm going to tackle later.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: But let me just ask if we can get a report, Mr. President, latest update vis-a-vis the passage of our Government Optimization Act.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Kasi dun sa Government Optimization Act, the Government Optimization Program covers all agencies of the Executive, including GOCCs.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Yan po, yung pinakita kanina ni Sen. Lacson, yung mga non-performing, except eco-zones, covered noong Government Optimization.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Baka pwede makahingi tayo ng report, update on what we are doing, especially focusing dun sa mga non-performing.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Yes, Secretary Kim, can you provide the committee of the information?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, your honor, as to the Government Optimization Program,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we have actually identified 15 GOCCs, some of those are included in the list to be covered by the GOP.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And as far as timeline is concerned, the deadline for these agencies to submit the respective Government Optimization Plan, your honor, is in fact August 29.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So, after August 29, we expect to receive all the proposals from all these agencies, GOCCs and NGAs included,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: as to how they intend to optimize the respective operations of the agencies, your honor, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Next to answer, Senator Riza, next to ask questions.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: Mr. Chairman, can I just ask, not ask, quick comment.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: Quick comment with the permission of Senator Riza.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: On the top of the list was duty-free Philippines.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: Like, everybody wants to go duty-free shopping.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: Sinabi na lang, sinabi na lang ng Governor of BSP that we are a consumer, ano?

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: With the permission of Senator Pia…

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: I went there like two weeks ago, nobody's there.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Dito sa malapit sa airport, nobody's there.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: And I asked why, because of the dollar rates.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Mr. Chairman, I just need to clarify, that's our list.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: And I just asked my staff, sigurado ba tayo dyan, sigurado pa naman.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: At the top, and to note, in other Asian countries na nabibisita natin,

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: ang dami pa nilang duty-free shops.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: Outside of the airport, outside of the perimeter of the airport.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: And then, we're a consumer country daw.

segments.speaker: Senator Pia S. Cayetano
segments.text: So, yun na nga ang buhay natin.

segments.speaker: Senator Panfilo Lacson
segments.text: Siguro, pa-validate na rin natin sa kanila, Mr. Chairman.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Please, Secretary Kim, please validate itong concern nila.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, your honor, looking at the list, Mr. Chair, your honor,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: if we will look at the subsidies column, if the figure in the subsidies column is zero,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: that means, your honor, we don't provide any subsidy from the GAA.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But we understand that the table might be presenting GOCCs under two different classifications.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: One is an asking GOCC that receives subsidy from the GAA,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and another one who is non-asking but also incurring net losses.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Ang bottom line, yung binabanggit natin kanina, yung mga government employees,

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: for example, sa duty-free, pumunta ko kayo doon, wala ko silang ginagawa.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Nakatambay lang po silang lahat doon.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: Dahil wala naman hong namimili eh.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: So, again, ang point nitong budget hearings natin is to make government offices more efficient, Mr. Chairman.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: That's a good thing that we were able to tackle it.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I think, ang sagot dyan, all of the items now are available elsewhere, you know,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and then malls, anywhere, and cheaper.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, probably, it's one of the reasons.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Ma'am Yun, now have the floor.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Catch up ako sa DepDev, yung presentation kanina.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: SecRC, sabi nyo po kanina sa presentation nyo na para makabawi yung ekonomiya natin itong susunod na taong 2027,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: kailangan mag-focus tayo sa mga high-impact projects tulad ng catch-up, infra-projects,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: at saka buffer stock para sa agri-inputs.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Kaya lang, sa 2027 NEP, nasa 1.1 trillion, sa kabuwa ang 7.1 trillion na budget,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: ay nakalaan para lamang sa pagbayad ng debt interest payments.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Di pa nga sa principal, sa interest pa lang.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The first part of your question,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: on the high-impact projects that we need to speed up for implementation,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: tama yan, I think the infrastructure has a very high multiplier effects.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and so this help employment and help consumption and help improvement,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and other indicate dimensions of welfare.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Now, of course, the budget for 2027, we hope that we can move in that direction.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: But as we mentioned earlier, Madam Chair, Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to us, even if we see a slight decline in the total amount,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: for, say, for infrastructure, as long as the quality is so much improved,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I think we can still get better impact.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And we have, of course, the experiences in recent quarters involving corruption scandals

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: tell us that there's a lot of things that can be fixed to help improve that quality that I'm referring to.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: My colleague could answer the interest payment issue.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: But before we move to SecGo, Mr. Chair, kaya ako tinanong po sa DepDev.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Because kahit makapagpatayo tayo ng, sabi niyo nga, mas kaunti pero mas quality na infra,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: hindi pa nga natin na pag-uusapan yung buffer stocks sa agri-side,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: And if we spend about one-seventh nung budget next year para lang sa debt interest payment,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: naturally, mababawasan yung para sa infra, mababawasan yung para sa agri.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: In fact, mamaya, napansin ko nga po, no, yung budget na kalaan sa pambayad ng interest pa lamang ng utang natin,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: mas malaki na dun sa budgets para sa health, agri, at saka social services, all put together.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: 1.1 trillion pambayad ng interest payment kumpara sa mas maliit na pagsuma nung tatlong.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Pero, so, kinoconfirm nyo po, 1.1 trillion para lamang bayaran ng interest ng utang natin?

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I don't have the figure with me, Mr. Chair, but of course, my colleague here has that about that.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: But I think that what I would like to note, Madam Chair, in response to that,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: is I think that interest payments are obligations that we have incurred.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And I guess you have to ask whether postponing or even asking for deferment of the payments will work in a longer term better for us than paying those obligations now.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: As we try to do a more efficient fiscal programming so that we don't compromise the quality spending of the entire government.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And my own sense words, Mr. Chair, is that I think that it's very important that the investment community would see us as a country that respects contracts.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And that we, to the extent that those obligations have been incurred,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I think, but how we finance that, that would be my colleagues at DOF as what is the most efficient way of raising the revenue to finance the payments

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: because there are ways of addressing that issue without compromising.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: And finally, Mr. Chair, before we move to Sego and before the Chair himself interjects,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: kaya ako po tinatanong kasi kahit naman sa household,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: level, binabalansi talaga na minsan kailangan nating umutang.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Pero may priority tayong pagkakagastusan pa rin.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, kaya ako tinatanong itong anlaki ng porsyento ng budget para next year sa pagbayad sa interest ng utang.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: And then it will impact dun mismo sa sinisabing yung pambawi natin sa ekonomiya, no, infra, and then yung agri nga.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: And bago tayo dumako kay Chair and then kay Sego,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: so kasi paano nga natin masasabi na...

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Kung mas kaunti yung budgets ng health, agri, at social services na pinagsama

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: kesa pa yung item natin pambayad ng interest sa utang.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, paano natin masasabing people-centered pa rin yung ganitong klaseng budget?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: I think gaya ng argument na sinabi kanina ng my colleagues that

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: there is so much scope for improving the quality of spending

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: so that we can still deliver.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Even better services, whether these are for health, for education, for social protection,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: even as we are constrained with the total amount.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: I guess, I think this is very important moving forward that when we borrow,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: and which will result in interest payments later,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: we do make sure that what we borrowed is invested, is used properly,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: so that it generates much higher value than what we pay later on

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: in terms of interest payments and amortization.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: But I guess if the experience in the last three quarters,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: or what we have seen in the scandals,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: is that we have borrowed, put them in places where they didn't seem to contribute

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: to higher capacity for the economy,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: then that's really the wrong and inefficient way of using financing.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Before I give way for the interjection of the chair,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: precisely, may mga corrections talaga na kailangan namin gagawin dito sa proposed budget.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Scandals aside, at tinututukan din niya ng Senate, pero a much better budget pa po.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Yes, we need to have just...

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Senator Diveros, I'll try to interject.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Same point po, the DBCC can answer, of course.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: At one point, does DBCC consider itong interest expenditure a serious constraint on development spending?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Parang ano na tayo lagi, parang we're always looking at itong ating financial standing, debt servicing,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: to the point na parang we are already sacrificing.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Parang isa ka talaga bali sa akin, or...

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: If I may, for me, from a development perspective, Mr. Chair,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: it doesn't hurt to pay interest payments if the amount we borrowed was able to generate far more incomes

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And amortization that we paid for.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: So, we incur interest payments, and those interest payments can rise, but if we are able to guarantee

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that those yield better results for the economy, then that should not be a concern.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, we have not become too focused naman on keeping our finances in order, that we have

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: under-invested in infrastructure, kasi parang nahuli na tayo eh.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We're just spending on average of 2% through the how many decades as compared to our ASEAN

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: neighbors who are spending 5% or more.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, but now, a little bit higher, tumaas ng 6%.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Previous administration, bumaba na naman ngayon.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, yun lang ang concern natin.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Probably later on my timeline, I would just pursue this.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: To SECGO, yung debt ng bansa natin ngayon, 19.07 trillion pesos.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: At lambas na po ito sa end of year, 2026 targets, at nasa Agosto pa lang po tayo.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, maaari nyo po bang i-detalye kung aling mga agency programs ang nabawasan

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: ng mga budgets dahil sa lumiit na fiscal space natin ngayong taon?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, I'm confirming that our total debt today is 19 trillion pesos.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But when it comes to the budget, I would have to defer to my colleague from the DBM to answer.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Before we move, Mr. Chair, to Secde Leon, would the Secretary like to comment on how can we call this a people-centered budget?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Kung mga one-seventh ng budget ay gagastusin natin sa debt interest payments pa lamang.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: than all the budgets of health, agri, and social services put together.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, if I can answer from a fiscal point of view,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: which is why I am a strong advocate of fiscal consolidation.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: When the administration started, the deficit to GDP was 7.3%.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We've narrowed that down to 6.2%, then 5.7%, last year 5.6%,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and this year we are trying to target 5.45% deficit to GDP.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Which means that we are becoming more efficient in collection of revenue.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And ideally, we start looking at our expenditure to spend smartly rather than volume.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: It's the quality rather than the volume.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And I just want to point out that as far as expenditure goes,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: if I compare to our regional neighbors, roughly, I'm oversimplifying the numbers,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: but if our revenues are roughly 16% of GDP, we are at par or better than our neighbors.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: However, our expenditure at 22% of GDP is much higher than our neighbors.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So, hence, we are creating a deficit,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: which is why the economic team has created a fiscal framework, a plan, a path,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to keep reducing that fiscal deficit.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And as pointed out by my colleague earlier, these are already obligations of the government.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: When the administration started, we had a total of 12.8 trillion pesos already in debt.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We had to start with that.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And hence, we need to maintain our good credit rating globally,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: which will allow us to borrow, continuously borrow, to fund priority programs of the government.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But, Secretary, since the brand of the budget for next year is a people-centered budget,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: when can you start really using...

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the higher levels of revenues of our economy?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: For, first of all, the urgent recovery of the economy,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the infra and buffer stocking for Agri, high impact.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And then for the priority programs that are being called,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: it was proposed that the health, Agri, and social services will be smaller.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So, we can't recombine compared to the item for debt interest payments.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Even year-on-year, can't we adjust that to make the pesos and centavos really clearly more people-centered

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: while not completely letting go of our obligations to be good debtors?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: I believe that when we said that the budget is people-centered,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: that means that the budget was very well scrutinized and chosen

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: so that the projects and programs that the government will implement

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: are those with the greatest multiplier effects,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: On your question of changing our debt obligations,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: but doing a better balancing act of using yung sinabi nyo,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: vis-a-vis GDP as compared to our regional neighbors,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: using those revenues more for the high-impact projects na pambawi sa economic downturn natin,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and then also for the developmental and social protection programs,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: then parang priority kasi kung sa absolute numbers lang,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: priority to pay yung debt interest,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: I think the DBM is in a better position to explain the process of how they come up with the budget,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: but I believe there are contractual obligations or automatic appropriations

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And I believe that interest payments, the NTA,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the NTA is even higher, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: but the NTA is 1.3 trillion this year.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So all the automatic appropriations are allocated first,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: if I may use that term.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So it's an automatic appropriation, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: and partly that's our historic problem about automatic appropriations.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: But sige po, dumako tayo kay Sec de Leona.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: how the budget is proposed to Congress.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: But can you tell the committee better,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: paano natin tatawagin pa rin itong people-centered budget,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: given the way the proposed appropriations for the different items stack up

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: well, as mentioned by the Secretary of Finance,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the premise why we are saying that the budget is still people-centered

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: is precisely because the biggest chunk of the budget

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: will still go to the people-centered budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: It will still go to the social sector taken together.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And when we look at social sector,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: even housing and other social services.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: And again, this sector receives the biggest chunk of the budget,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: hence that we gave the priority to this sector.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But then again, if we compare it to our 2026 level,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: there might be some nominal decrease,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: precisely because of some inefficiencies encountered

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: by the implementing agencies for their current year's budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: To name a few, Your Honor,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: for health, HFEP, for agriculture, farm-to-market roads,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: all of these are infra which are not fully implemented

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: even at the middle of the year.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: That's why this is a major consideration

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: while we have continued to provide budgets for these programs for 2027.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The amount is not at the same level

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because precisely, the remaining balance by the end of this year

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: will have to be carried over for 2027.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: One thing we'd also like to highlight, Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: is that for 2027, we tried to do some correcting measures

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: in terms of addressing some spending inefficiencies.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We noted during our presentation before we had lunch

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to cover for PS and MOOE requirement,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: which is not always the case in the previous year's budget.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So that actually raises some concern

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: on possible sustainability of implementing a budget

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: wherein we take on additional borrowings

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and yet we just borrow for our regular operating requirements.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So at least the parameter that we use as the economic managers

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: is that if we resort to borrowings,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: at least it will go to high-impact infrastructure

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: projects that will give us greater return

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: than the interest that we'll be paying eventually

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to our creditors in the long term, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: so given nga yung automatic appropriations,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: results also, especially in years like this one,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and yun na nga na-exceed nung interest payments,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: pwede nyo pa bang i-detalye sa committee

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: dahil dito sa lumiliit na fiscal space natin

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: aside from the three items that I have already mentioned,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: they receive a lower amount for the 2027 NEP

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: if we compare it to the 2026 GAA

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: precisely because of the continuing balance that they receive.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We also noted, Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: that there is also an observed decrease

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: in the level of the budget for some of the subsidy items,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: If we compare the 2027 NEP level

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: but why are we proposing a decrease?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because precisely, Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: and I believe this is also something that we have discussed

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: with the new Secretary of Health

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: when he was still President of PhilHealth,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we also have to address the spending inefficiency

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: as envisioned by the universal healthcare law

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: will not be competing from the same basket,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: from the same pool of resources.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So while there is a decrease

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: in terms of the MAIFIP level of DOH,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: there is an increase that we provided to PhilHealth

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: precisely to cover the continuous implementation

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: but also including local government hospitals alone.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because we see investment to PhilHealth

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: also as investment to all our hospitals

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: because definitely the fund that we provide to PhilHealth

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: will eventually be cascaded to our hospitals.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Another one with a reduction, Your Honor,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: if we compare from the current year's GAA budget

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: one-off reduction from the Office of the President,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: attributed to our ASEAN hosting this year.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So we have provisions for ASEAN hosting for 2026

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: which will not necessarily be needed anymore for 2027.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: I note ko lang, Sek, at Mr. Chair,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: bagamat pinopropose niyong dagdagan ang PhilHealth

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: pero may double whammy pa rin on the health side

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: dahil parehong you propose to reduce the funding,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: including to HFEP and pati sa MAIFIP,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: both institutional and social protection input

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: sa kabuang pag-achieve natin ng universal healthcare.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: But I'm sure the Chair and I and other colleagues here

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: will work on that at the proper time.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: If I still have time, Mr. Chair,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: gusto kong balikan yung slide number.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: With the indulgence of our distinguished guest.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: sa big cut on the education budget for CHED and SUCs kasi.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: SUCs about 3 billion from last year in the NEP

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: and then for CHED, I think at least about 15 billion.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: But anyway, I'm not going to pursue that right now.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
segments.text: I know this is not my time.

segments.speaker: Senator Joel Villanueva
