segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: One is the national government debt, and second is our general government debt.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The general government debt, which is –

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The general government debt, which is the global standard to be used, is roughly around 58 percent today.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Is the 60 – that's a different – I think – what is the – in the – well, anyway, so 58 percent.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Now, I understand there's a – generally, when it – right now, of course, we're investment-grade.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But generally, there's some – there's a threshold, or maybe not necessarily just debt-to-GDP.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But, I mean, there is a point.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: There is a point where we don't want to pass – where we don't want to exceed, because it might affect our investment-grade status.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And I just want to ask, what is that – more or less, as a general, what is that threshold that we do not want to exceed?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: There is a World Bank threshold for general government debt-to-GDP that they have now put a number to, which is 70 percent general government debt-to-GDP.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So we have a space of about 11-plus percent.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So are we looking at – are we looking at – what trajectory are we looking at heading into – based – of course, this – the budget this year was based – or for next year was based on certain projections.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So based on that, what are you projecting for our debt-to-GDP for the following year?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We're projecting to go from 58.6 now to 58.4 to 58.3, all the way down to 56.1 by the year 2030.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And the reason why I'm asking also is, you know, I think the fiscal space is important.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But, you know, of course, aside from the debt increase, it's important that – what is our GDP target?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Because this is – I mean, what is our – because obviously, debt-to-GDP, we're not just talking about – I mean, the GDP increase will be very relevant to this number.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So obviously, if our debt is – if our GDP is far outpacing our debt, you know, we should be – there shouldn't be many issues.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But if we have a – if we continue on this low GDP, it might – it might bring us to a level that we would not want.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: In real terms, Your Honor, the target GDP growth for 2027 and 2028 is 5.6.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: That's the target for this year.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Ah, that's the target for next year.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: For this year, what is the target?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And in terms of GDP growth, what – how is the – where did we see a drop?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Was it in consumption, government spending?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Was it in – which portion of the formula for GDP?

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: It's everywhere, except for net exports.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Exports grew faster than imports, which is quite different this time compared to previous years.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Personal consumption dropped quite to something like 2 point – it slowed down – it slowed down to roughly just a little above 2 percent in the last quarter.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: What do you attribute the drop in personal consumption?

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: It – earlier I mentioned the weakening of – the weakening of GDP.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The weakening of consumer sentiments arising from the acceleration of inflation in March, which continued – it diminished a bit, but it's still 6.2 percent as of last July.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: That's still quite high compared to 2 to 3 percent – or 2 to 4 percent target.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And so – and also the – I mentioned also about this concern about governance issues, the perception about our institutions and governance, and I think that that affected particularly the investment side of the equation.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Yes, and even the – I believe the government spending side is also quite sluggish.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The public construction contracted by over 30 percent in two successive quarters.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: The reason why I also want to segue into –

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I have been helped by the law to raise the exemptions to the income tax ceiling, 300 to 360,000 pesos.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: In my mind, if – if the government spending is low – government spending,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: and the consumption is also low, I just – I thought that this – raising the income tax ceiling will give additional income to the lower – I guess the mid-to-lower earning segment.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So I thought that maybe this is a way – in my mind, it's also a way of prime-priming this.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And it's – in a way, instead of helping, it's also good to lower the income tax for those who – who are not doing well.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So I think that if the government spends a lot of money, maybe it's also a way of prime-priming this.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Maybe it's also a way of prime-priming this.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So I think that if the government spends a lot of money, maybe it's also a way of prime-priming this.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: for those who are earning less, for the lower, I guess, the lower-earning income segments.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And that will translate to a direct benefit in consumption

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: because that's obviously, instead of us giving out ayuda, an exemption on income tax,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: while it will create a fiscal, I guess it will take a hit in terms of revenues,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: but it will be compensated by an increase in consumption.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I suppose. I mean, I would surmise.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Can I ask your comment on this?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I'm curious because this is a bill that I filed,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: and I wanted to know what the fiscal repercussions of this bill are,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And the consumption effects, I think that those certainly will be positive,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: but I think the ayuda that we are talking about here,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Or the effects of the tax exemptions would not reach many of the poor

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: who are in the informal sector, who are not paying income taxes to begin with.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And many of them are poor in that category.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: So I think what we have seen in the last, particularly during the 2023 to 2025 period,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: which is the period where we have data,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: show that when done well, the ayuda could actually help,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: especially those who are victims of circumstances like floods or typhoons.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Actually, I'm not saying that there should be no ayuda.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: The ayuda is okay, I'm just saying.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Maybe it's also good that we also have the lower income segment.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: We don't have what we call D, E.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: We also have the lower income segment.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Maybe we also need to give relief.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And in my opinion, income tax is also a big relief for people earning less than P360,000 a year.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Generally, these are people who do pay taxes.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: They're minimum wage earners who pay taxes.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But if we can give some of them some tax relief,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: in my opinion, it's not just...

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I understand that there's something right in the government's revenues.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But at the same time, this is a way of giving instant relief to many of our taxpayers

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: who also need a lot of our low-income tax earners.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I hope you can maybe compute what the net benefit is if we lose some of our revenues.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: At the same time, may madadagdag din sa consumption.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: For me, it's a progressive reform.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Hindi na natin pipiliin kung kanina natin ibibigay yung ayuda.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Ito directly to people who need immediate relief, I think.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So, I want to ask your comments, Mr. Chairman, on these thoughts.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The net benefits, I don't think that the first-round effects on consumption,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: additional consumption and additional revenue that that consumption would generate,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: would be able to offset what you give away.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Do we know how much more or less revenues is generated?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: What would be the effect on our revenues of that tax like that on the lower-income segment?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Since that's directly a DOF question.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: I think, for example, in our proposal to raise the personal income tax exemption to 350,000 a year,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: we're estimating to lose about 60 billion in taxes.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And we will probably recover only somewhere around 15% of that in taxes.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The reason for that is the highest level of consumption at that income bracket will be food.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And a lot of the food-related are exempted, for example, from VAT, and there's a lot of exemptions at that level.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: That's why I think when it comes to...

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Of course, obviously, in the ecosystem of government, once you collect, you will have to redisperse it somehow.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: If the government spending is low, as it has been,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I was just saying, perhaps we might consider these tax exemptions as a more efficient way to give assistance to those who may need it.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Because it's, like, again, I said, in a way, we can see it as a little bit more progressive.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: It's not bound by inefficiencies in distribution or bureaucratic inefficiencies.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: It's just a clear cut that goes directly to the spending.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: to the income of our lower earning, lower income segment.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So I just hope this is something that we can compute.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I hope I can ask, maybe the effect is 60 billion,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: but I mean, when you talk about in a nationwide scale,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: there are a lot of people who will benefit from this bill.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Of course, in terms, it is so immediately, and it's immediate.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: You don't have to wait for it to be distributed, there's no bureaucracy.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: The moment you pass this bill, immediately, those who are earning less than 30,000

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: will have immediate relief to many people.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So I hope that can be given a very strong consideration,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: and hopefully, you can support the bill.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Because I think there's something right, but for me, it's also worth it.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Maybe from our GCCs, if we can generate 60 billion from our GCCs,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: and we can pass this bill, I think it would be great

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: if we can increase the income tax exemption ceiling.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So I hope that can be considered by the economic team.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I think another way of looking at it is,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the tax rates was 2018, was it?

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And there has been so much inflation since then.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: You see, so that those groups of population in that bracket

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: are now paying much higher, effectively, much higher taxes than in 2018.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So in a way, it's an inflationary adjustment.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: That's a good way to look at it, Secretary.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: actually this bill is just adjusting it to the realities of the past years of inflation.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: That's a very good way to look at it, Secretary.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So maybe as part of the,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I hope that the Department of Finance will also consider that as a,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: it would be a big, I think it would be,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: a big help to our countrymen.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And this help will be given immediately.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So it's a big deal if we pass this bill.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Defended a few years ago is the Maharlika.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Gusto ko sanang humingi ng update kung ano po yung mga investments ng Maharlika

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: at kung ano ng performance ng Maharlika Investment Fund.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: principal investments of the Maharlika Investment Corporation as of June 30, 2026

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: They've invested 1.17 billion in Synergy Grid.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: They've also invested 8 billion in Asian Terminals, Inc.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: They've also lent working capital to Petron Corporation of 15 billion.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: This was during the height of the oil crisis and a small investment in a mining company.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: What's the name of the mining company?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But I believe this has already been unwound.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: It wasn't exactly a convertible bond.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: It's like a loan that is convertible...

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So they converted it to equity?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: They actually sold it at a profit.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And the Maharlika has declared a dividend, I understand, already?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Yes, they declared a dividend this year.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And this represents a rate of return of what?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Well, the total capital invested there was 75 billion pesos.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So they have not deployed all the capital yet?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But I suppose the rest, they invested it in T-bills?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So the other ones, why have they not been able to deploy?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: I believe, Your Honor, that they spent a lot of time and resources on trying to close a deal with...

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: A larger deal with the grid.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Yeah, they spent a lot of time and resources in trying to close a larger deal with Synergy

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Grid, or the grid, the transmission company.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: However, they were not able to close the deal with them.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But this 1.17 billion that you see that I mentioned earlier is actually them participating

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: in the equities market, which actually, I must say, has also...

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Made quite a good profit for Maharlika.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But yes, it's very small compared to the deal they were seeking.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: That's about a 2-point-something percent yield, I believe.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But it sounds like it's 2-point-something percent, I believe.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Well, they only remit to the national government 50%.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: This is just the dividend yield.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Their real profit is higher than what they give back to the national government as dividends.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And the dividend is the whole year?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Or maybe it's just for the first quarter or first half of the year?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: It's for the whole year of 2025.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Are we expecting a higher dividend yield for the next year?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: I can say that with quite certainty, yes.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But do we have a projection for that?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Or not at this moment your honor

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: But there's no deals in the pipeline?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Every time the board meets, they actively discuss two or three deals.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But being a sovereign wealth fund, they're also, I think, probably on the conservative side.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So the deals don't come as quickly as it would in a private company.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Can I request, Mr. Chairman, maybe for all of us, an update on the...

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And I think I discussed it with the Senate President.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Maybe we can ask for an update, a more specific update of what's happening with the Maharlika.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And we're hoping, of course, that it can generate also some additional revenues in the short to medium term.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So, Mr. Chairman, can we ask for an update?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Can we maybe request an update for all of us?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: An update from Secretary Deco about the plans of Maharlika?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We will be at your disposal when you schedule that briefing on Maharlika.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And we will have the President and CEO of Maharlika as well as other officers.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Yes, please have him accompany you during the proper budgeting of the DOF and other agencies as well.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Likewise, with the indulgence of Senator Mark.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: One of the intents of the Maharlika was really to pursue about...

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Will you still pursue about the acquisition of the shares, supposedly of the state grid, the NGCP?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: At this point, the talks are not progressing as well as we hope it to be.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But I will not say that it's completely not...

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So, I think Maharlika will continue to pursue a potential investment in the grid.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: That is the owner of NGCP, one of the synergies.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So, there is an investment of 1.7 billion?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: SGP, which is Synergy Grid, is a listed company owned by the Filipino shareholders in the grid.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: It's an investment, but the investment is small for NGCP indirectly through the local investor in NGCP, correct?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The shares were bought in the open stock market, in the Philippine Stock Exchange.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Because they're a listed entity in the Philippine Stock Exchange.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: So, what you mentioned, I guess last year, their acquisition of NGCP or Synergy did not continue?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And finally, my last is regarding...

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: As an author of Afasa Bill, I would like to thank BSP for mentioning Afasa Bill earlier.

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: And I just want to know what are the updates, if Afasa Bill helped in enforcing anti-scamming,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: Have you caught a lot of scammers, or has the performance of BSP improved because of Afasa Bill?

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: I just want to know, as I want to know what are the updates, if it helped, and if it helped,

segments.speaker: Senator Mark A. Villar
segments.text: what is the extent of improvement in our enforcement?

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: Allow me to answer that question.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: Since I'm the General Counsel of BSP, and under me, under the Office of the General Counsel,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: under the direct supervision of the General Counsel, is the CAPO, the unit that was created

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: pursuant to the AFASA, so that's the Consumer Account Protection Office.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: And to respond to your question, Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: it helped, it was a big help for AFASA, if you ask us at BSP, in enforcing anti-scam and fraud.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: In fact, in terms of the...

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: in our efforts to implement the AFASA,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: there are already cases of finiles

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: In fact, we've been coordinating with law enforcement agencies,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: we're able to, you know, the bar use or several law enforcement,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: agencies were able to file cases.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: I know in December 2024, for example, the NBI, the National Bureau of Investigation,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: arrested seven Chinese nationals involved in an online scamming operation in Paranaque

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: for offenses that included social engineering schemes under AFASA.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: The PNP, the Philippine National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group, or ACG,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: of which 447 had already been solved or cleared,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: and noted a decline in online scam incidents during the first half of 2026,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: which is partly attributed to increased public awareness of fraudulent schemes.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: we at the BSP, again, through the CAPO,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: we have actually entered into information-sharing agreements

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: with different government agencies or law enforcement agencies

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: like the SEC, the CICC, and the Department of Justice in this year, 2026.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: Our invitation there, Mr. Chair, is, again,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: again, thank you for the effort.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: Thank you for the efforts of the sponsors, the senators who sponsored this AFASA bill.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: One thing that we are able to do now because of the AFASA

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: is that CAPO is able to look into the bank accounts of these scammers and fraudsters

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: that previously were not able to do.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: We don't need a court order to be able to do that.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: And because of these additional powers and functions given to us,

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: Nakakapag-share po kami ngayon ng mga information na maaring magamit ng mga law enforcement agencies sa paghabol po dito sa mga fraudsters and scammers.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: And of course, more importantly, tumaas po yung probability na ma-recover po ng mga biktima ng fraud at scam yung perang nawala po sa kanila.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: So ginagawa po namin itong ISA, Information Sharing Agreement, as I said, with the different law enforcement agencies and other government agencies

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: para po rin masigurado na kung ano man yung information na makuha namin at i-share sa kanila ay hindi po na-abuso at nagagamit lamang po sa tamang paraan.

segments.speaker: BSP General Counsel Roberto L. Figueroa
segments.text: Kaya again, as I said, to respond to your question, malaki pong naitulong at marami pong salamat doon po sa pagpasa po ng batas na iyon.

segments.text: So we also intend to integrate information from the Subay Bayan portal into COMPASS

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: so that we can give our citizens a comprehensive information

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: as to the status of releases and implementation of LGSF-funded projects, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: The LGSF has two components. One is the RISE, one is the INFRA.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Well, there is a menu, Your Honor, but what we are seeing right now, the trend,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: is we are giving focus on RISE at one end and the rest of the infrastructure from the menu on the other end.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: I would assume that the RISE is because of inflation.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Because of the erosion of purchasing power.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: It's the result of the Middle East crisis as well.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Correct. So we're giving RISE so that it's a caution to the reduction of purchasing power.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: The INFRA is supposed to stimulate construction nationwide.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Correct. So I'm very interested with the INFRA because rinitain yung 57,

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: So yung ibig sabihin, naging maganda yung experience ninyo,

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: And that's what I want to learn.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: You mentioned the word sustained gain.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: So I want to see a study that there was a gain.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: May gain na nangyari sa mga LGUs.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: And that's why it led you to repeat it again in 2027.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Prior to that, maliliit lang yan.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Pero ngayon, naging quadruple yung amount niya.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: So you don't have to give it to us today, but just submit to us through you.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: A study in which the LGSF stimulated growth in the countryside,

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: helped our LGU achieve their developmental goals,

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: kung kaya, reduce poverty, improve educational outcomes,

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: We want to learn how LGSF helped our LGUs and their constituents.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: And with that, Mr. Chairman, I don't have any more questions.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, yes, thank you, our Senate President.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Actually, nag-overtime kami para hindi na kayo bumalik bukas.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Kahit mag-late tayo, at least you don't have to return tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, our last to, ano, no?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Actually, dapat si Senate President has the priority,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: but he chose to let everyone.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, our Senator Tiberos, please, you have the floor now.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, gaya ng sinimulang kong itanong kaninang umaga,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: kailangan paghandaan natin yung El Niño.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: ito yung magiging pinakamatinding El Niño

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: sa loob nitong nakaraang ilang mga dekada.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, unang tanong po, dito sa 2027,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: magkano pong nakalaan para mapaghandaan ng,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: well, lahat ng Pilipino, lalo na yung mga magsasaka natin,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: ang El Niño at malampasan yung mga magiging epekto nito sa atin?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: And across agencies po, kung maaari, yung nakalaan.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Actually, Your Honor, we have started preparing for the possible effect of El Niño

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: as early as now because we have actually captured the possible effect,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: of El Niño, under the uplift framework.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: That is why we have facilitated some augmentation to the Department of Agriculture

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to start front-loading some farm inputs because they tried to change their planting calendar.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Inurong nila ng isa o dalawang buwan, ano po?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Yes. So, we have provided some augmentation, Your Honor, on additional inputs,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: both on the fertilizer side, but also supporting,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: even the fuel requirements of our farmers, so that's under the uplift framework.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So, we're not waiting for 2027. So, we've started working right now.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Before you continue, Sec, but dahil nga dinilay nila yung pagtatanim by one to two months,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: kailangan paghandaan din, maybe even still using the uplift framework,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: yung insecurity sa food security dapat dahil sa pagdilay ng planting?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We fully note that, Your Honor. So, uplift is still ongoing.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: In fact, while it hasn't been disbanded, so the interventions continue.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So, that's on the farmer side, not only on the fertilizer, but even their possible fuel consumption.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We're even looking at support, possible support for forms of irrigation.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So, we're looking at different irrigation projects that would also include exploring solar irrigation

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So, we are utilizing not extraordinary line items.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: As a matter of fact, DA is maximizing its existing line items as a matter of front-loading,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: prioritizing as well the beneficiaries, but we also have on standby the NDRIM fund

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: for any possible shortfall that may arise if the regular funding sources under DA

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: would not be enough, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Magkano lahat-lahat yung naka-allocate proposed sa 2027 budget para doon across agencies?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Kahit isubmit nyo na lang po in writing sa chair, yung breakdown per agency.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Yes, pero may ballpark figure po ba magkano lahat-lahat kahit across agencies, pero yung suma

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: para sa El Nino response and preparations?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Because our current risk resilience data, Your Honor, is not just exclusive to El Nino.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So, maybe we have to disaggregate.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Maybe attributable programs and projects for El Nino alone.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Pakisubmit na rin yun in writing kasama nyo doon sa chair.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Follow up po sa current 2026 budget naman, anong available resources ang ginagamit natin

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: ngayon para sa buffer stocking ng bigas at pati repair ng mga rainwater catchment facilities

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: or water storage facilities in general?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: For buffer stocking of rice, Your Honor, and if...

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: The NFA is utilizing its existing budget as part of its mandate for the repair of rainwater

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: collection facilities, I believe DPWH is using available resources including their regular

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: budget for repair to rehabilitate if there are damaged facilities for that matter, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Pakisubmit na rin in writing yan, Secretary, para sa pag-interpolate namin doon sa agent.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, amid the global trade policy uncertainties, I think around the table, sa ayan tayong lahat,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: we really need to bring in those foreign direct investments into the country.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, tanong po pareho sa DOF at saka sa DEPDev rin, paano tutugunan ng proposed 2027 budget?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Yung constraints, mga constraints sa pagpasok.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Noong mga gusto nating foreign direct investments yan.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Particularly, yung constraints ng napakamahal na kuryente, doubling cost of logistics,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: at yung pagiging puno o crowded noong mga ports natin.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Would the DOF like to address that or DEV?

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I, Mr. Chair, and Your Honor, earlier I flashed the amendment,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: law amendments that we would like to be prioritized by Congress,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and one of that is the EPIRA, because that will go a long way in reducing cost of energy in the longer term.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And we are talking about a more effective ERC, better coordination between ERC and PCC in going after abuse of market power,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: as well as investment in downstream and upstream in the energy sector.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I think that the waste of energy is also a high priority that we are asking Congress to pay attention to, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: And in addition po sa legislative, kasi shop naman namin yun, pero dito po sa proposed 2027 budget,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: paano ini-intend na ma-address itong mga constraints?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: From the executive side naman po.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I think we are focusing on, as we said earlier, on the more efficient bureaucracy.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I think the ease of doing business that we need to keep improving because the World Bank report still puts us,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: identifies the ease of doing business, particularly permitting...

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And the regulation of the various agencies have made it, still make it so difficult to do business in the country.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: So, I think we are mindful of that support for our bureaucracy.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Sek, what about yung problematic ports natin?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: At saka yung napakamahal na logistics?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: May proposed spending items ba kayo sa proposed 2027 budget para i-address yun?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Yeah, logistics and for agriculture, for post-harvest facilities, that's quite, I understand, high in the agenda of Department of Agriculture.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: And I think that our colleague in DBM can provide the numbers, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Your Honor, Mr. Chair, I completely share your desire to increase investments in the country.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: As a matter of fact, that's practically what I was doing for the first two years I was here in government.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And I think the answer lies in policy reforms.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: They're not, unfortunately, I don't think they'll be found in the budget.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But they revolve around two things, the ease of doing business and the predictability of doing business.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Fortunately, in the first two years of mine in government, I worked with the legislature and we passed several very good reforms like the Create More Act, the PPP Code, the Accelerated Right-of-Way Law, and the Mining Fiscal Regime, as well as the Land Lease Act.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So I think those are all very good laws.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: that ensure the ease of doing business and the predictability of doing business.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But they're really not found in the budget.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: There is one agency that you're probably referring to if you're talking about increasing the number of ports in the country, and that would be the PPA, the Philippine Ports Authority.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: First of all, on PPA, we do not provide subsidy to them, I'm told by the DBM, because they have their own revenue source.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: They take care of their own port projects.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But specifically on the crowding of ports, and if you're referring to the customs, the crowding of containers in the shipyards, that is a very serious concern.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: What I have been told is that in the last two administrations, so probably 15 years running, they've been trying to solve this problem.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And I think we're now in the midst of probably passing a joint

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: I think we're now in the midst of a joint administrative order where we are dividing the territory, if you will, between the ships that belong to Marina.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And as soon as you unload the container from the ship, it now belongs to the Bureau of Customs territory.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We hope that if we can finalize that joint administrative order, we'll be able to resolve this issue.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Because there's a gray area in the ports of...

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Which agency is responsible for what?

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: In addition to resolving that or making clear that gray area, Sec,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: ang laking bagay halimbawa kung DA natuloy yung kanilang unang magandang plano to build yung mga cold chain storage facility sa lahat ng ports at lahat ng airports.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So siguro pagdating sa pag-examine namin sa agency budget ng DA,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Lastly, Mr. Cherque, salamat si Sec, RC is raising his hand.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: I wanted to go back to him nga.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Sa planning inputs po kasi ng DepDev for the 2027 budget, meron ba kayong inputs noon regards these constraints to bringing...

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: yung FDIs, yung mahal na kuryente, yung mahal na logistics, at saka yung baradong mga ports?

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Oh, maybe I can come later because I would want to raise an elephant in the room.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Because we talked about food security a lot and we have seen that food inflation

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and high cost of food in the country is really a major issue.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: It has made the price of food in the country is almost twice than what you can get in Vietnam or Thailand or Indonesia.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This is really a very serious problem on food security.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And that cuts across our social fabric, education, health, and so on, and the competitiveness of our workers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I look at the census of agriculture.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Do we know, for example, that because we don't have a national land use,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that we have been trying to ask the Congress to pass a national land use for the past quarter century,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: there were 9.67 million hectares of agricultural land.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: By 2022, there are only 6.31 million hectares.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Or we lost 3.4 million hectares of land.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: there are about 3.13 million so-called irrigable areas.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I mean, those lands that have potential for irrigation.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: But only 1.84 million of that is irrigated.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: it's almost exactly the same amount at the same level of irrigation.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: you have not made them productive by building the proper irrigation.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Now, rice production in the last 10 years grew by only 0.9% every year.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Our population is growing at 1.23% average per year.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: So, are we surprised why we are importing so much?

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: where we have allowed our very productive farms

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: you see irrigated lands being converted into,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and that's something that you cannot see

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and you don't see in Thailand or Vietnam.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: My colleagues in Vietnam told me that

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: if you are looking for the root problem

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: of our incapacity to produce enough food

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: We haven't made our farmlands more productive

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: by investing in their productivity-enhancing measures

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And we haven't passed a national land use code

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to rationally manage our land resources.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that will be a game-changer for this country

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: if this Congress can finally pass a law,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that has been languishing for the last 25 years.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Isabit ko na lang sa inyo in writing

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: because, sorry po, I need to leave.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: na dagdagan yung mga tanong ko

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Last na lang for the record, Mr. Chairman,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: ito pong mga constraints na to,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Ito ay masasagot ng isang mga agensya.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Ito ay masasagot ng isang matatag

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Naging simula na yung tatak Pinoy,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: At kasi, ayon sa mga sagot

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: and when that new oil crisis erupted,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: at inabsorb natin yung parehong shock na yun

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: Sila nagpakita ng higit na kahandaan,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, ito po yung mga bagay

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: dahil gusto po namin dito sa Senado

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: o isang budget na may proactive na plano.

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: So, maraming salamat po, Mr. Chair,

segments.speaker: Senator Risa Hontiveros
segments.text: at maraming salamat sa ating mga resource persons.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The Chair just has some concerns.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: but just to set the record,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: How much of the projected revenue increase

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: in the government's real revenue capacity?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Our tax revenues is projected to grow

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: If you look at the GDP projections

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: there is a little bit of buoyancy

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So, if you assume the low end of both,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: then there's a little bit of buoyancy

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Also, likewise, DOF is targeting to raise

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, how will we ensure that the assets

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: that we will receive will be disposed

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Won't this privatization be used to address

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The privatization efforts of the government

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the reason why we were more confident

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: from the privatization of the CBK,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: We have already sold it, Mr. Chair,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: instead of a fair market value

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Now, we don't own the whole building,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Sa joint vent, parang ano ba yan?

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The exact number is we own...

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: was equivalent to a billion pesos.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, thank you for clearing that.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: if you'll allow me to answer this,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, ito po may mga questions.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: It can be very easily managed by the country.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: However, if we maintain our fiscal deficit at 5.5% or more,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: then we will see that more and more of our revenues

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: or more and more of our expenditure will be going to servicing debt.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Last but not the least, health budget and rising prices.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Of course, I'm very much concerned because this concerns budget of DOH and PhilHealth,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: which of course are the NGC's primary that will implement universal health care.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The DOH budget is projected to decline by 11.4%,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: while the government subsidy to PhilHealth is projected to fall by 42.6% to 74.4 billion.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Take it together, national government funding for health would decline by 20.8%

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Question is, why is the government reducing health sector funding

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: at a time when inflation is increasing the cost of health care

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and placing the greater pressure on household incomes?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: Mr. Chair, Your Honor, again, one of the factors that we have considered

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: in terms of the level of DOH in particular,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: are possible continuing appropriations that will spill over until the next year.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: A significant portion would be the Health Facilities Enhancement Program, or HFEP,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: which is still unutilized at this point by the DOH,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: as well as some additional MOOE provisions for operations of the hospital.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: But as the Chair has already noted, the reduction for PhilHealth is mainly attributed

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: We have a $60 billion that we returned, but with the discussion,

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: we will be sitting down with Secretary Edwin Mercado and President Beverly Ho

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: on how we can work on the $19.8 billion variance to cover what's supposedly earmarked

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to PhilHealth without sacrificing, of course, because it will be a zero-sum game.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: There will have to be some agency who will experience some sort of a $19.8 billion reduction

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to accommodate the same to be transferred to PhilHealth, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Well, we'll definitely be monitoring that, and hopefully we will be able to support that

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: because I think it will be very important now to really...

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Since the President also mentioned that zero-balance billing and other benefits of PhilHealth will improve,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: so we're not so sure that we will also...

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We will do our part also in scraping the barrel, so to speak.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I just want to bring it up that one problem with the...

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Zero-balance billing and the improvement of the PhilHealth's coverage,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: the medical inflation, there are some.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I brought this up with the meeting with the DOH and the PhilHealth.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, hospitals, doctors, they said that the payment of PhilHealth is slow.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: They have increased the professional fees and other expenses.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, the previous one, for example, 5 million or 10 million per LGU that is being given assistance for them,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: it used to be long, but now it's just a little because hospital bills have an average now.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, that's why I brought this up that now that the medical inflation is a problem,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I think the timing of reducing the funding for the health sector might not be a good idea.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I think the budget of the agencies themselves, especially DOH, will try to resolve this.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Last is, does the DBM and DOF consider the remaining PhilHealth reserves sufficient to sustain benefits and services

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: despite the lower government subsidy in 2027?

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: In fact, we are cognizant that there are previously issued allotments that remain unfunded.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: At this point, we're working on a workable, on a viable solution, of course, mindful of

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: the deficit level that we also have to maintain.

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: So we maintain close coordination, Mr. Chair, with PhilHealth to ensure that they will continue

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: to provide the benefits that is approved by PhilHealth without really affecting or putting

segments.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
segments.text: so much pressure on the deficit level that we have.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So, with that, we would like to fast-track our briefing.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We will send to the concerned agencies the rest of my questions for their appropriate

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: responses, and also, before we end, I would like to put on record that Senator Alan Caetano,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: our minority leader, also sent his questions for the DBCC, which we'll furnish you, and

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: we will endorse this to each of the agencies for their appropriate responses.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: With that, we would like to thank our colleagues.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: patiently waiting for the return to ask

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: questions, as well as our economic

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and for responding to the questions of our

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: concerns, we will no longer request you

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you again for your time.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: So pasensya na kung humaba, at least you don't have to

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: have any more questions, again, this

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: briefing is hereby suspended. Thank you. We'll see
